text:
Traditionelle Chinesische Medizin (TCM) wird oft als eine unveränderte Heilkunst aus dem Altertum dargestellt.

Historisch betrachtet ist die Realität komplexer.

Viele Heilpraktiken wie Kräutermedizin oder Akupunktur haben tatsächlich sehr alte Wurzeln in China. 
Das moderne System „Traditional Chinese Medicine“ entstand jedoch erst im 20. Jahrhundert, als verschiedene medizinische Traditionen zusammengeführt und standardisiert wurden.

Heute wird TCM weltweit genutzt und umfasst viele unterschiedliche Methoden. Einige pflanzliche Wirkstoffe aus der traditionellen Medizin wurden später wissenschaftlich untersucht und sogar zu modernen Medikamenten entwickelt.

Gleichzeitig sind viele Konzepte der TCM wissenschaftlich umstritten oder schwer nachweisbar.

Die Geschichte von TCM zeigt deshalb auch, wie Medizin nicht nur durch Wissenschaft entsteht, sondern auch durch kulturelle, politische und gesellschaftliche Entwicklungen.

Quellen:
Hsu, E. (2008). The History of Chinese Medicine in the People’s Republic of China.

Taylor, K. (2005). Chinese Medicine in Early Communist China.

World Health Organization (2019). WHO Global Report on Traditional and Complementary Medicine.

post_owner.name: DR. ROSEY LATHOURAS (Chinese Medicine)
text:
One thing I often hear is: “I don’t believe in Chinese Medicine.”
But medicine isn’t really about belief — it’s about observation, outcomes, and ongoing research.

Traditional Chinese Medicine developed through thousands of years of clinical observation. Practitioners recorded patterns, responses to treatment, and how the body changed over time. Long before modern laboratories existed, physicians were already studying how different interventions affected real patients.

Today, modern research is beginning to explore many of these traditional practices more deeply. Acupuncture, for example, has been investigated in hundreds of clinical trials, particularly in areas such as chronic pain, migraines, musculoskeletal conditions, and nausea. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses continue to examine where it shows measurable benefit and where more research is still needed.

Like many areas of healthcare, the evidence is not uniform across every condition. Some treatments have strong research support, others show promising early findings, and some still require more rigorous investigation. This doesn’t mean the medicine is invalid — it means the scientific process is still catching up to centuries of clinical practice.

Research evolves. Our understanding of the body evolves. And good medicine stays curious, open, and willing to investigate new questions.

The most important thing is supporting each individual body with care, attention, and the best knowledge available — both from modern science and from the clinical traditions that came before it.

Find a registered practitioner, give it a go!

Depression, for example, is described as an imbalance of the organs, almost always involving the liver.

• Worry: stomach and spleen

As always in Chinese medicine, prevention is better than cure and knowledge is power.

text:
THE ARMY AND THE OSCARS - MAJOR FRANK CAPRA 

"I’ll make you the best damned documentary films ever made.” - Major Frank Capra

Academy award-winning director Frank R. Capra joined the Army on 12 December 1941, a few days after the attack on Pearl Harbor and U.S. declaration of war against Japan. Granted a delay in reporting for active duty to complete editing on the movie "Arsenic and Old Lace," he was commissioned in the Signal Corps on 29 January 1942. 

Chief of Staff General George C. Marshall selected Major Capra  to produce a series of documentaries that chronicled the war as it was fought. According to Capra's memoirs, Marshall said, "... I want to nail down with you a plan to make a series of documented, factual-information films – the first in our history – that will explain to our boys in the Army why we are fighting, and the principles for which we are fighting." 

Although a successful director of entertainment movies in civilian life, he purportedly told the chief of staff, "... it’s only fair to tell you that I have never before made a single documentary film.” The general answered, "Capra, I have never been chief of staff before. Thousands of young Americans have never had their legs shot off before. Boys are commanding ships today, who a year ago had never seen the ocean before.”

Capra recalled that he replied, “I’m sorry, sir. I’ll make you the best damned documentary films ever made.”

Under Capra, the Army's Special Services Motion Picture Production Unit made the award-winning documentary series "Why We Fight." The first film, "Prelude to War," won the Academy Award for Best Documentary in 1942. 

Capra returned to the film industry after completing his wartime Army service. His Oscar was returned to the U.S. Army in a ceremony in Los Angeles in 2008.

The military received two other Academy Awards for documentaries, "Seeds of Destiny" (1946): Produced by the War Department and "Toward Independence" (1948): Produced by the Army.

🍃 Cold Weather Exercise Recovery — What Does Your Body Need?

Ever go for a run or workout outside in cool weather and come back with a runny nose, scratchy throat, or fatigue?

In TCM, when we exercise, our pores open as we sweat. This temporarily weakens our defensive Qi, making it easier for wind, cold, or dampness to enter the body. The body just needs a small adjustment with warm foods, teas, or soups to rebalance (do this immediately after as not to let the pathogens go further in).

❄️ Wind-Cold invasion = runny nose, chills, sneezing, stiff neck. Cold wind enters the body while the pores are open during sweating. Goal: Release the exterior and warm the lungs

• Ginger + Green Onion Tea: Fresh ginger + green onion whites simmered for 10 mins
• Chicken Ginger Soup: Chicken, fresh ginger, red dates boiled med heat for 1.5 hrs
• Ginger + Red Date Tea: Fresh ginger + red dates gently simmered 10 mins

🌬️ Cold + Lung Dryness = dry throat, slight cough, mild thirst. Cold air can dry the lung fluids during exercise, especially when breathing heavily outdoors. Goal: Warm and gently moisten the lungs

•  Pear + Red Date Tea: Snow pear + red dates simmered for 10 mins
•  Snow Fungus Pear Soup: Snow fungus, pear, goji berries simmered for 20 mins
•  Goji + Honey Tea: Goji berries + warm water + honey steeped

💧 Qi & Fluid Depletion = fatigue, dizziness, dry mouth after sweating. Prolonged or intense exercise can temporarily deplete Qi and body fluids. Goal: Rebuild energy and restore fluids

• Ginseng Honey Tea: American ginseng slices + honey steeped
• Dang Shen Chicken Soup: Dang shen, chicken, red dates boiled med heat for 1.5 hrs
• Goji Berries + Red Date Tea steeped

🌫️ Wind-Damp Exposure shows up as heavy body, thick mucus, foggy head when exercising in cold AND humid conditions. Goal: Transform dampness and move Qi

• Chen Pi Ginger Tea: Aged tangerine peel + ginger boiled 10 mins
• Fu Ling Pork Rib Soup: Fu ling, pork ribs, ginger boiled med heat for 1.5 hrs
• Rose buds + Chen Pi steeped

Don’t let the weather stop you! Stay strong!

O tribunal também estabeleceu que a administração municipal deverá comprovar a devolução do montante aos cofres públicos.

Liver myths I hear all the time.

The first is that the liver detoxes itself and you don’t need to do anything.

The liver is always working.

The second myth is that the liver can regenerate no matter what.

The liver does have remarkable regenerative capacity. It’s one of the only organs that can regrow tissue after injury.

But regeneration has limits.

Chronic inflammation, fatty infiltration, alcohol injury, viral damage, and long-term metabolic stress all reduce regenerative potential over time.

Regeneration works best when the burden on the system is reduced.

Support matters.

morning – after lunch – before sleep.

text:
🌿 Such a small ingredient, yet so powerful in Traditional Chinese Medicine and Chinese cooking.

Lotus seeds (莲子 – lián zǐ) are neutral in nature and slightly sweet, making them incredibly versatile in soups, teas, congees, and dessert soups. They’re gentle enough for daily use and often show up in family recipes for digestion, rest, and recovery.

In TCM, lotus seeds are known to target the Spleen, Heart, and Kidney systems.

This means they are commonly used to support:

✨ digestion and weak appetite
✨ calming the mind and supporting sleep
✨ gentle energy rebuilding
✨ postpartum recovery
✨ stabilizing loose stools
✨ nourishing the body without being heavy
✨ vitality

Because they strengthen digestion while also calming the mind, lotus seeds are one of the few ingredients that support both the gut and the nervous system.

Before cooking, remember to soak dried lotus seeds for about 30 minutes. If you see the small green core inside, remove it — it can be quite bitter.

Here are a few simple ways to use them:

🥣 4-5 Lotus Seeds + 3 Dried Red Dates + 4-5 Dried Lily Bulb + 1 cup of water (as a tea, boil together for 10 mins): A calming tea or light soup that helps soothe the mind and support restful sleep.

🍚 8 Lotus Seeds + 1/2 cup of White Rice + 10 Goji Berries + 2 cups of water (boil together for 1 hour on med until rice becomes soft, stir occasionally): Make a nourishing congee for a gentle Spleen-supporting breakfast.

🍄 8 Lotus Seeds + 1 whole Dried Snow Fungus + 10 Goji + Rock Sugar to taste + 2 cups of water (boil together for 1 hour on med heat until snow fungus is soft): A classic sweet soup often used to nourish fluids and support skin hydration.

🍗 10 Lotus Seeds + 1 Whole Chicken + 10 Red Dates + 1 piece Chinese Yam + 2.5 L of water (boil on med heat for 2 hours): A beautiful soup for rebuilding energy and supporting postpartum recovery.

Explore lotus seeds here: https://thechinesesouplady.com/lotus-seed/

Usually a fan of the less-is-more approach, there are occasions when we have limited time and want/ need to cover more target areas in one sequence. If so, we might consider ‘stacking’ - to use the pose and ball to access more than one target area at the same time.

In this version of Dragonfly side bend the balls are placed along the same myofascial meridians as the tension being experienced in the Yin pose, to amplify the flow of Qi at the same time as releasing tension.

Dragonfly side bend is predominantly targeting the obliques, with the corresponding ball held in compression on the outer shin muscle (gallbladder meridian).

The second target area for the Yin pose is the hamstring of the opposite side, with the corresponding ball in compression behind the ankle (urinary bladder meridian).

Learning how to intelligently and creatively sequence MyoYin, can make or break a sequence.

This might trigger you, but your lifestyle isn’t separate from your condition. It IS the condition.
We say this with love. And we say it because no one else is connecting these dots clearly enough.
Here’s what we hear almost every day: someone comes in and describes their main complaint — migraines, chronic fatigue, digestive problems, inflammation. And then almost as an afterthought, they mention the rest.
“Oh, and I’m pretty stressed. Work has been insane.”
“Yeah, I don’t really sleep well. Haven’t in years.”
“My diet’s not great but I don’t think that’s related.”
Every single time, those things are listed like background noise. Like they exist in a different category than the “real” problem.
But what if they’re not background noise? What if they’re the main event?

text:
Your mouth is not just about teeth.
It’s one of the most underestimated gateways to your overall health.

In traditional Ayurveda, morning oral care is part of the daily Dinacharya — a ritual designed to remove toxins (Ama) and prepare the body for the day.

Thousands of years ago, Ayurvedic physicians already recommended simple practices such as:
• tongue scraping
• oil pulling
• cleaning the teeth and gums

The idea was simple: reduce bacterial load in the mouth before it can influence the rest of the body.

Today, modern science is beginning to confirm what ancient systems observed.

Research shows that chronic gum inflammation (periodontitis) is associated with a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular disease. When the gums are inflamed, oral bacteria and inflammatory molecules can enter the bloodstream and contribute to systemic inflammation that affects blood vessels and the heart.

Several large studies support this connection:

• A large meta-analysis found that periodontal disease is associated with about a 19% higher risk of future cardiovascular disease.
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12738947/

• Other studies report around 30% higher risk of myocardial infarction in people with periodontal disease.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11671167/

• Severe periodontitis has been associated with up to 49% higher risk of heart attack in some populations.
https://www.mdpi.com/2673-947X/5/2/14

In other words:
your gums are one of the few places where bacteria can directly access your circulation.

This is why oral care is not just cosmetic, it is part of metabolic, immune and cardiovascular health.

My morning routine follows a simple structure inspired by these principles:
– tongue scraping to remove overnight bacterial buildup
– oil pulling with coconut oil (rich in lauric acid)
– cleaning the interdental spaces where inflammation often begins
– brushing the teeth

Longevity beyond trends.
Resilience beyond hacks.

The Large Intestine meridian runs from the index fingers up the outer arms, across the shoulders and into the face, helping us process, clear and let go.

The poses above are some of my fav yin poses for this season and to gently stimulate these pathways:

Saddle Pose
A deep opening through the front body, lungs, belly and hip flexors, creating spaciousness for breath and circulation through the Lung meridian.

Heart Melting Pose (Anahatasana)
A soft surrender of the heart and chest toward the earth, encouraging breath to move into the ribcage while stimulating the Lung and Large Intestine channels through the arms and shoulders.

Bananasana
A side body stretch that lengthens the intercostal muscles between the ribs, giving the lungs more room to expand while gently activating meridian lines along the arms and sides of the body.

Autumn invites us to slow down, breathe deeply, and practice the quiet art of letting go.

text:
Mesmo com o aumento de vagas dos últimos anos, o déficit na educação infantil continua sendo um dos principais desafios de Anápolis.

Levantamento atualizado do Tribunal de Contas dos Municípios do Estado de Goiás (TCM-GO), em conjunto com o Ministério Público de Contas, aponta que o município precisa construir 28 novas unidades, entre creches e pré-escolas, para que a fila de espera seja zerada.

Segundo os dados do “Retrato da Educação Infantil 2025”, do Ministério da Educação, Anápolis teria atualmente 4.070 crianças aguardando vaga.

Para atender a essa demanda, o investimento estimado seria de R$ 163,6 milhões: o segundo maior do Estado, atrás apenas de Goiânia, que necessita de 50 novas unidades educacionais.

No cenário estadual, 31.324 crianças estão na fila em 125 municípios goianos. A estimativa técnica do TCM-GO indica a necessidade de 275 novas creches e ampliação de outras 52 já existentes, ao custo total de R$ 1,53 bilhão.

Apesar de ainda elevado, o número representa queda de 32% na demanda em relação a 2024, quando 45.976 crianças aguardavam vaga.

📙 Demanda seria menor em Anápolis

Em Anápolis, porém, os números geram divergência com a pasta local.

O Ministério Público da Bahia (MPBA), o Tribunal de Contas do Estado da Bahia (TCE) e o Tribunal de Contas dos Municípios da Bahia (TCM) assinaram uma Nota Técnica conjunta com diretrizes para orientar os municípios nas contratações de artistas para os festejos juninos de 2026.

O documento tem caráter orientativo e define parâmetros para pesquisa de preços, avaliação da economicidade e planejamento das despesas, com base na Nova Lei de Licitações e na Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal.

Entre as principais recomendações está que os municípios utilizem como referência a média dos cachês pagos aos artistas entre 1º de maio e 31 de julho de 2025, com correção pelo IPCA. Caso não haja dados suficientes, a pesquisa pode abranger os 12 meses anteriores, mediante justificativa técnica.

A análise dos contratos de 2025 mostrou que apenas 1% ultrapassou R$ 700 mil. Por isso, valores acima desse montante entram em “faixa de atenção especial” e exigem justificativa detalhada, comprovação da capacidade financeira do município e demonstração de que não haverá prejuízo às contas públicas.

Durante o evento, também foi lançada uma cartilha explicativa com orientações práticas para prefeitos e equipes técnicas, reforçando a necessidade de planejamento, transparência e responsabilidade fiscal nos festejos.

I used to have heavy, painful, irregular periods, acne, mood swings ➡️ I have a regular and painless period, clear skin, balanced mood 🥳

What helped me was:
1️⃣ Cycle syncing 💞
It took me a few months to get the hang of this, but seriously it’s the BEST thing a woman can learn.
You learn to get in touch with your cycle and plan your exercise, food, social outings, work and energy around your cycle. It’s amazing how much more energy you can have, how much more comfortable your body feels, and how much less you need to force.
WomanCode by Alisa Vitti @alisa.vitti really helped me!

2️⃣ Nervous system regulation 🧘‍♀️
This is honestly the root and key to everything! The nervous system controls the reproductive and endocrine system through the hypothalamic pituitary ovarian axis. When you are dysregulated, in go go go mode, stressed all the time, your brain prioritises survival over reproduction.
Chronic stress raises cortisol, disrupts ovulation signalling, affects insulin sensitivity and throws off estrogen and progesterone balance. So no wonder your organs start misfiring and things feel imbalanced!
There are many things you can do to regulate your nervous system. My favourites are breathwork, meditation, EFT, exercise particularly yoga, hypnosis and cold showers.
Art of Living SKY breath @artofliving is the one that has helped me the most. I still practice this daily.

3. Naturopathic and Ayurvedic herbs 🌿
The ones that helped me the most were Shatavari, Vitex also known as Chasteberry, and Ashwagandha.
(Please consult a practitioner, this is my personal experience only).

True healing isn't about masking the symptoms with a pill ... it was about getting to the root cause of the imbalance so that your body naturally heals itself!

post_owner.name: Dr Carla @ Adelaide Women’s Health
text:
E N D O  M Y T H S ‼️
|| Endometriosis is complex. It deserves nuanced, individualised and compassionate care. There is no one-size-fits-all solution.

This is why a multidisciplinary approach can really help. It all starts with LISTENING to endo sufferers & believing them, not dismissing them or putting them into a box. (Cue, Chinese medicine, a gentle, holistic approach that can help manage endo alongside other things). 

Some common MYTHS we need to put to bed:

❌ “Have a baby — it will cure it.”
There is no known cure for endometriosis. Pregnancy may change or reduce symptoms temporarily, but it does not cure endometriosis.

❌ “A hysterectomy fixes it.”
Endo is tissue outside the uterus. Removing the uterus doesn’t automatically remove lesions elsewhere. While a hysterectomy might relieve symptoms for some, it does not guarantee the disease will not return.

❌ “It’s just bad period pain.”
Debilitating pain is not normal. Missing work, vomiting, fainting = not “just a period.”

❌ “The pill will fix it.”
Hormonal suppression can manage symptoms. It does not cure the condition.

❌ “There’s nothing you can do except surgery.”
Endometriosis requires an individualised, multi-factorial, multidisciplinary approach. Surgery can help with symptoms but it cannot be promised as the be all and end all gold standard. 

❌”Endo is a gynaecological disorder”.
It not just a gynecological disorder, but rather a chronic, systemic, whole-body inflammatory disease that desperately needs more funding and research to be better understood and managed. 

Endometriosis is not caused by weakness.
It’s not cured by pregnancy.
And you are not dramatic.
You deserve informed, compassionate, + evidence-based care.
Xo ||

Comment YIN below for a link👇🏻 This all-herbal formula for ADHD has been in use for 1,000 years and was first developed by the esteemed pediatrician Qian Yi (1032-1113), author of the world’s oldest surviving pediatric text, predating the earliest European pediatric text by 300 years. It is available on our site 🪴

Originally developed to treat ADHD in children, this Yin-nourishing, Kidney-tonifying formula is now primarily used by adults and is said by some sources to be the most popular classical TCM formula in China today.

Historically, Liu Wei Di Huang (available on our site) has been used for treating inability to focus in children, and is a variant of a popular 3rd century formula called Jin Kui Shen Qi. The pediatrician Qian Yi removed the two warming herbs and formulated this variant formula specifically for children, who did not require the warming effect of the herbs Gui Zhi and Fu Zi. (However, those who experience low energy, cold hands and feet, poor digestion, and poor memory may do better with Jin Kui Shen Qi.)

Many of the positive effects of Liu Wei Di Huang derive from its principal herb, the powerful adaptogen Shu Di Huang or prepared rehmannia. This herb is considered an important mood-regulating plant with a long history of use in psychological disorders and recent research pointing to its pronounced anxiolytic effects. You can find more research on this herb by searching by its Latin name: Rehmannia radix preparata.

Liu Wei Di Huang is also well-known today for its use in treating Yin deficiency, including mental irritation, feeling over-heated, dryness throughout the body, light-headedness, night sweats, and insomnia.

In Chinese medicine, what is known as the Kidney organ system is regarded as the root of Prenatal Qi, or “vital life force,” which plays a significant role in the formation of marrow, bones, teeth, and brain. Because of this, brain-based disorders are considered to be related to the Kidney system. Note that this term is not synonymous with kidneys in anatomy.

Vielleicht schröpfst du schon, oder du überlegst gerade, damit anzufangen – dann bist du hier genau richtig.

Was ist Schröpfen überhaupt?

Schröpfen ist eine Art Negativmassage. Du nutzt Unterdruck, um deine Haut nach oben in ein Schröpfglas zu ziehen.

Was dabei in deiner Haut passiert:
Durch den Unterdruck entstehen winzige Mikroverletzungen. Das klingt dramatisch, ist aber gewollt: Dein Körper startet dadurch Reparaturprozesse. In der mittleren Hautschicht werden die Fibroblasten aktiviert – die Zellen, die Kollagen, Elastin und Hyaluronsäure bilden.

Das Ergebnis: Aufpolsterung, Straffung und Durchfeuchtung von innen. Etwas, das keine Gesichtscreme der Welt leisten kann.

Aber: Die Technik muss stimmen. ⚠️

Wenn du falsch schröpfst, kann das Gegenteil passieren: Dauerentzündungen in der Haut, nachhaltig geschädigtes Gewebe – und am Ende wird die Haut schlaffer statt straffer.

Deshalb ist es super wichtig, die Technik wirklich richtig zu lernen.

Die Vorteile (wenn du es richtig machst):
→ Geht super schnell
→ Nur 2-3x pro Woche nötig

text:
One of my favourite cough remedies uses ingredients I almost always have at home. It’s gentle, simple and perfect when everyone in the house is coughing.

What to do:

• Slice one red onion thinly.

• Add it to a shallow pan with just enough water to cover the base.

• Bring to a gentle simmer.

• Leave for 3 to 5 minutes, until the onion starts to soften and looks a little squishy.

• Take the pan off the heat and remove all the onion, keeping only the liquid.

• Pour the liquid into a mug.

• Add 1 teaspoon of olive oil and 1 teaspoon of honey.

• Stir well and sip while it’s warm.

I like using red onion because it’s naturally a little sweeter and easier to drink, but white onion works too if that’s what you have.

The aim is simply to draw all the goodness out of the onion into the water and turn it into a gentle, soothing syrup.

It doesn’t taste as oniony as you’d expect and it’s one of my go to remedies when coughs are doing the rounds.

Before we replace hormones, we should first ask a deeper question:
Are we creating the biological conditions for hormonal health?
Vitamin D is one of the most overlooked hormones in modern medicine.
It regulates the immune system, inflammation, and plays an essential role in the hormonal axis.

Yet vitamin D deficiency is one of the most common deficiencies worldwide — especially in people living under chronic stress or with immune dysregulation.
Without sufficient vitamin D levels, the body simply struggles to produce and regulate healthy hormones.

And there is something even more fundamental: light and nature. Morning sunlight supports vitamin D production and helps regulate the nervous system.
Most people also don’t realize that certain sunscreens can reduce vitamin D production in the skin by up to 99%.

But hormonal balance is not only biochemistry.

When cortisol remains chronically elevated, something many modern women experience, the body often produces less estrogen and progesterone.

This is where ancient wisdom quietly enters the conversation.
In many Asian cultures, women historically relied far less on hormone replacement therapy and reported fewer severe menopausal symptoms.

Lifestyle played a role.
Daily movement, time outdoors, strong social connection, and a deep sense of purpose — what the Japanese call Ikigai.
Purpose, gratitude, connection, and positive self-talk stimulate hormones like oxytocin, which counterbalance stress hormones and help create a more harmonious hormonal environment.

This post is not against hormone replacement therapy.
Modern medicine can be incredibly valuable.
But sunlight, movement in nature, stress regulation, emotional wellbeing, and purpose are foundational biology.

Ancient traditions understood this intuitively.

This happens when your body has been under prolonged stress or emotional pressure, disrupting the smooth flow of energy.

This is very common during perimenopause and menopause. 
 
Yin represents your body’s cooling and calming energy.

This type of anxiety often worsens with sugar, caffeine, and alcohol.

Then there’s Blood Deficiency Anxiety.
 
This occurs when your body isn’t producing enough blood to nourish your brain and settle your spirit. 
 
You may appear calm and functional on the outside, but internally feel shaky, fragile, and easily overstimulated. 
 
This is the type of anxiety that wakes you up in the middle of the night with a pounding heart—even when nothing is “wrong.”

– vermoeidheid na het eten
– extra uitputting rond de menstruatie

De Miltfunctiekring is verantwoordelijk voor het omzetten van voeding in Qi en Bloed. Wanneer die functie verzwakt, blijft er als het ware “restmateriaal” achter. 

In TCM noemen we dat Damp.
Damp is één van de pathogene factoren binnen de Chinese geneeskunde.
Als dit langere tijd aanhoudt, kan Damp zich opstapelen en klachten verergeren zoals:
– hardnekkige vermoeidheid
– een zwaar gevoel in lichaam en hoofd
– gewichtstoename
– vochtretentie
– mist in het hoofd
– meer slijmvorming
– hormonale disbalans

Wat begint als lichte Miltzwakte kan 
zich dus verdiepen als je het signaal blijft negeren.

Herstel begint vaak eenvoudiger dan gedacht: warme, gekookte voeding, regelmaat in maaltijden, rust tijdens het eten en minder koude belasting voor het systeem.

Je tong laat zien wat je lichaam al langer probeert te vertellen.

post_owner.name: The Chinese Soup Lady
text:
🧧Wishing everyone a healthy, happy, and prosperous year of the horse! 

🌺Turn your Chinese New Year leftovers into a nourishing, healing Chinese soup! In this video, I show you how to make a simple and traditional Cantonese roasted pork soup using leftover siu yuk (燒肉), green radish, carrots, corn, honey dates, and apricot kernels. This is one of the most classic and foundational soups in Cantonese cooking — efficient, deeply nourishing, and perfect for everyday wellness.

🈵From a TCM perspective, this soup is slightly cooling and helps clear internal heat, support digestion, nourish fluids, and gently moisten the lungs. It’s especially helpful after festive periods like Chinese New Year when we’ve eaten more rich, fried, and heating foods.

This soup is perfect for:
• Clearing internal heat after eating fried or rich foods
• Supporting digestion and relieving bloating
• Moistening the lungs and helping dry throat or dry cough
• Nourishing fluids and relieving dryness
• Gentle daily nourishment for the whole family
• Reducing food waste by using leftover roasted pork

Green radish (青蘿蔔) regulates qi, aids digestion, and clears heat. Honey dates (蜜棗) gently nourish yin and moisten dryness, while apricot kernels (南北杏) support lung health and respiratory function. Combined with the protein from roasted pork and natural sweetness from carrots and corn, this creates a balanced, restorative soup suitable for regular consumption.

🌿 Ingredients:
• Leftover roasted pork (or your pork of choice)
• 2 fresh green radish, peeled chopped
• 2 fresh carrots, peeled chopped
• 2 fresh corn
• 3 dried honey dates
• 1 teaspoon of mixed apricot kernels
• 2.5 - 3 L water

When your soup water boils, add all the ingredients together. Boil on high for 30 minutes and reduce boil for another 1.5 hours or use a thermal pot for at least 2 hours. Salt as needed. Serve and enjoy!

text:
Thinking about stepping on the bodybuilding stage? 

The physical aspect is only half the process. Before you even pick a show here is a crucial reality check, does it fit into your life?

This isn’t about questioning your ambition to step on stage….it’s about building a rock-solid foundation to ensure you don’t just start your prep, but finish it successfully and with your well-being intact (just about lol).

A lifestyle audit is an honest evaluation of your life before the unnoticed demands of contest prep take over. It’s a game changer for anyone balancing a career or family, and absolutely essential for first-time competitors who might underestimate the sheer dedication required.

So, what does this look like?

First, your support systems. Your prep will impact everyone around you. Have open and honest conversations with yourself and then your family, bf / gf, and friends. Your social life will change, your mood will fluctuate, and your diet will be strict. Will they understand when you can’t go out to eat? Will they be the ones talking you out of competing based off what they’re missing out on, not what you’re missing out on. 

Next, the financial commitment. Competing is expensive, and the costs go far beyond a gym membership. You need to budget for coaching, posing sessions, entry fees, your tan, posing trunks / bikinis, travel, and food. Being financially prepared means you can focus on your training without the added stress of unexpected cost.

Finally, and most critically, your time availability. Be brutally honest with yourself. A successful prep demands a significant time investment. Between hours of cardio and actual gym sessions, meal prep, posing sessions, and getting enough sleep for recovery, your schedule will be mental. Map out your week and identify exactly where these non-negotiable hours will come from.

It’s about making an informed decision and setting yourself up for a successful and positive prep experience, which you’ve heard me say over and over!!

Saya sering dengar pasien bilang,
“Dok, katanya saya Qi stagnation.”

Dan saya selalu berhenti sebentar.
Karena itu bukan diagnosis medis.

Di literatur klasik TCM, Qi stagnation dipakai untuk menggambarkan keluhan yang terasa nyata, menetap, tapi sering sulit dijelaskan secara organik.

Kalau saya baca ulang dengan pendekatan medis, pola keluhannya sering berkaitan dengan:

• gangguan regulasi saraf otonom
• dominasi simpatis kronis (mode stres terus-menerus)
• ketegangan otot dan fasia
• penurunan aliran darah lokal

Ini bukan bukti bahwa “Qi” adalah entitas biologis.
Ini upaya mencari mekanisme yang bisa diuji secara fisiologi.

Tapi penjelasannya harus berdiri di atas ilmu yang bisa kita pertanggungjawabkan.

Kiinalaisessa lääketieteessä jalkoja pidetään tärkeänä energiakeskuksena.
Jalkapohjasta alkaa Munuaismeridiaani (Kidney), joka liittyy elinvoimaan, palautumiseen ja uneen.

	•	varastoivat Jing-energiaa (syvin elinvoima)

post_owner.name: Wurzelweisheit
text:
Diese schwarze Paste ist mehr als nur ein Aufstrich. Sie ist pure Nährstoffkraft aus der Natur. 💚

In der Traditionellen Chinesischen Medizin gilt schwarzer Sesam als „blutnährend“ und stärkend für Leber und Nieren. Er liefert natürlicherweise Eisen, Kupfer, Zink, Calcium und B-Vitamine. Nährstoffe, die für Blutbildung, Zellschutz und gesunde Haarwurzeln wichtig sind. Kupfer spielt eine Rolle bei der normalen Pigmentbildung der Haare (Melanin). Eisen trägt zur normalen Bildung roter Blutkörperchen bei.

🖤 Rezept (2 Zutaten)
• 80 g schwarzer Sesam
• 2 EL hochwertiger Honig

1️⃣ Sesam in einer Pfanne kurz anrösten (bis er leicht knistert).
2️⃣ Abkühlen lassen.
3️⃣ Im Hochleistungsmixer oder mit starkem Gerät fein pürieren, bis eine cremige Paste entsteht.
4️⃣ Honig unterrühren.
5️⃣ Im Glas kühl lagern.

Warum mixen?
Durch das Zerkleinern kann dein Körper die enthaltenen Nährstoffe besser aufnehmen als bei ganzen Samen.

💡 So kannst du sie verwenden:
• Als Brotaufstrich
• Als Topping für Porridge oder Joghurt
• In Smoothies
• Als gesunde Dessertbasis

1 TL täglich reicht völlig aus.

⚠️ Wer sollte aufpassen?
• Bei Sesamallergie natürlich meiden
• Bei stark erhöhtem Eisenwert nicht übertreiben
• Honig nicht für Kinder unter 1 Jahr

Natürlich süß. Mineralstoffreich. Sättigend. Und für viele eine echte Alternative zu stark verarbeitetem Schokoaufstrich.

Speichere dir das Rezept und probiere es aus. 🖤

In Western medicine, chronic fatigue can become frustrating especially when your blood work looks “normal,” but you don’t feel normal.

It’s a sign of deeper underlying imbalances.

The most common one is Qi and Blood Deficiency.
 
Qi is your body’s energy. Blood nourishes your organs, tissues, and even your emotions. 
 
Think of them as your body’s fuel supply. 
 
When you don’t have enough qi and blood, it’s like running on half-charged batteries.

This type of fatigue often gets worse after meals and around your period. 
 
You may struggle with brain fog, poor memory, dizziness, or feeling easily drained by small tasks.

The second imbalance is Dampness.
 
Here, you technically have energy—but it’s trapped in a swampy environment. 
 
You feel heavy, sluggish, and lethargic, almost like you’re wrapped in a damp towel. 
 
This fatigue is constant and sticky. 
 
The more you lie down, the more tired you feel.

The third type is Liver Qi Stagnation, or stress fatigue.
 
In this case, you have energy—but it’s blocked. 
 
You might feel the urge to take deep breaths often. 
 
Sometimes you feel temporarily energized after crying, releasing emotions, or even after a heated argument. 
 
Once the emotional pressure releases, your energy flows again.

Ginger has long been used in Chinese Medicine as a natural antibiotic and to support our Lungs as its warming properties help dispel cold and dampness in the body.

Ginger tea is also a fantastic remedy for nausea, so it’s worth trying if you have morning sickness or are recovering from a stomach bug.

Bu fonksiyonlar; bedeni sıcak tutma (ısıtma), metabolik süreçleri yönetme (dönüştürme), kan ve sıvıları hareket ettirme (hareket), organları yerinde sabitleme (koruma/tutma) ve dış etkenlere karşı savunma sağlama (bağışıklık) olarak özetlenir. Savunma (Wei Qi) Fonksiyonu: Cilt ve mukozayı güçlendirerek bedeni dış etkenlere (virüs, bakteri vb.) karşı korur.

post_owner.name: Niall Kenefick - Physique Coach
text:
Peak week isn’t a magic formula.

It’s not “cut water Thursday, add salt Friday, carbs Saturday.”

It’s assessment / adjustment / reassessment.
Day by day. Sometimes hour by hour.

Too many people think peak week is about doing something extreme.

It’s not!!

It’s about doing the right thing at the right time based on what’s in front of you.

You dont make changes based off what other clients or coaches are doing, it’s all based off the individual in front of you and what’s needed in that moment. 

Every decision from more carbs, water, sodium, steps, pump session the week of should be a reaction to real-time feedback.

Some situations you need to push food. Some you need to pull back. Some clients need aggressive loading. Others need barely anything at all. 

Peak week is not about doing more. It’s about doing less but doing it right. 

Fat loss is over at this stage, the smallest reduction in stress can make the biggest changes in someone’s look.

A lot can change over a matter of days, even with the smallest changes to food, water, output. 

If you’ve done the work for 16–20+ weeks, your condition should be there. That’s the goal isn’t it?

The best peak weeks I’ve coached were “basic”, small adjustments based off what’s in front of me and what my client gives me feedback wise. 

At this stage of your prep you should have a solid idea of what’s needed to fill someone out, how their weight tapers after a number of high days and so on…..

Gather the right information as early as you can in prep and you’re setting yourself up for success.

Jedes Mal, wenn du in etwas Knackiges beißt (Karotte, Apfel, Nüsse), arbeiten deine Kaumuskeln mit ziemlicher Kraft.

Dieser Reiz geht über den Trigeminusnerv direkt in den Hirnstamm – dort, wo u. a. Muskeltonus, Haltung und Schutzreaktionen mitgesteuert werden.

Mehr bewusstes Kauen kann helfen,

	•	deinen Kiefer besser zu nutzen statt nur zu pressen,
	•	die Knochen und Strukturen rund um den Kiefer sinnvoll zu belasten,
	•	und deinem Nervensystem klare Signale zu geben:
„Ich bin im Körper, ich verdaue gerade – nicht nur im Kopf.“

	•	viele Sorten enthalten Süßstoffe & Zusatzstoffe, die nicht jedem gut tun

Dauernd zu kauen, ohne wirklich zur Ruhe zu kommen, passt oft zu einem System, das sich permanent durchbeißt.

text:
Wir sind keine Maschinen.
Aber viele von uns leben, als wären wir es.

🧠 Der Kopf ist voll,
das Nervensystem ausgedünnt,
der Körper angespannt,
innen fühlt sich alles nach „zu viel“ an.

Nicht dein ganzes Leben umkrempeln.

Let’s talk about the three main categories of swelling:

1) Physiological swelling
This is temporary — after salty food, poor sleep, heat, or before menstruation.
You drink warm water, move your body — and it goes away.
This is normal fluid fluctuation. The system is still working.

2) External swelling
This is surface level — from wind, cold, dampness, or sudden climate changes.
In TCM, the Lung system controls the skin and pores and regulates the surface.
If defensive Qi is weak, fluids don’t move correctly.
You may see puffy eyelids, light facial swelling, sensitivity to cold or wind.
This type usually improves with warmth, movement, and circulation.

3) Internal swelling
This is deeper.

If you drink warm water, exercise, and massage your face — but swelling keeps coming back — the issue is internal.
In TCM, fluid metabolism starts in the center: the Spleen and Stomach system.
When the abdomen is cold, tense, or stagnant, fluids are not transformed properly.
Dampness accumulates — and one of the first places it appears is the face.

So sometimes the solution is not more facial massage.

It’s restoring the center — with abdominal work, arm work along the Lung meridian, and yes, moxibustion can be very helpful too. I’ll talk about moxa in a separate video.

text:
Buiten wordt het lichter, de dagen worden zachter, en toch voel jij je niet meteen energieker. Integendeel. Je lichaam voelt wat zwaarder, je hoofd iets voller. Je vertering is gevoeliger dan normaal en je bent sneller prikkelbaar. Alsof je systeem nog niet helemaal mee is met de lente.

In de Chinese geneeskunde zitten we nu in de periode van Yu Shui, Regenwater. Dit is het moment waarop Yang langzaam begint te stijgen na de winter. De natuur komt in beweging, de Lever-Qi wordt actiever en er ontstaat meer dynamiek in het lichaam. Tegelijkertijd is de kou nog niet volledig verdwenen en neemt de vochtigheid toe.

Deze combinatie van stijgend Yang en aanwezige Damp maakt dit een instabiele overgangsfase.

Wanneer er meer vocht in de omgeving is, wordt vooral de Milt functiekring kwetsbaar. De Milt houdt niet van Damp en ook niet van koude voeding. Als ze verzwakt raakt, zie je klachten zoals een opgeblazen gevoel, zwaardere ledematen, losse stoelgang of een soort loomheid die niet verdwijnt met slaap.

Tegelijk beweegt de Lever functiekring actiever. Dat kan emotioneel voelbaar zijn: sneller geïrriteerd, ongeduldiger, gevoeliger voor stress.

Veel mensen denken dat dit hét moment is om te detoxen of volledig over te schakelen op rauwe voeding. Vanuit TCM is dat niet aangeraden. Te veel koude en rauwe voeding verzwakt het midden nog meer, waardoor Damp zich makkelijker opstapelt en vermoeidheid blijft hangen.

Voeding tips:
Warm en licht verteerbaar eten, soepen, gestoofde groenten, granen zoals rijst of gierst.

Leefstijl tips:
-Voor 23u naar bed gaan zodat Yin beschermd blijft terwijl Yang begint te stijgen. 
-Zachte beweging in plaats van intensieve training. Wandelen, qigong, rustige yoga.

Als je je midden nu ondersteunt, kan de Lever Qi vrij bewegen zonder chaos te veroorzaken. Dan groeit je energie mee met het seizoen, in plaats van dat je erachteraan blijft lopen.

Sla dit op als herinnering voor de komende weken🌱.

#tcm #ChineseGeneeskunde

post_owner.name: Dr. Jonathan Kukor, DTCM, CMTPT
text:
You’re not a list of hacks. You’re a human being.
Somewhere along the way, wellness became this game of collecting fixes. One hack for sleep. Another for energy. Something for your gut. Something else for your joints. A nootropic for your brain. A supplement for stress.

And every single one of them sounds great in isolation. “Oh, this is good for me. This can do that.”

But here’s what nobody stops to consider — none of these things are working together. You’ve turned your body into a science experiment with 20 different variables and no control group.
That’s not a wellness plan. That’s chaos with good intentions.

In this conversation, we talked about something that honestly shifts the entire way people think about their health: what happens when you stop trying to hack individual molecules and processes, and instead just get your whole system working in concert?

Because your body isn’t a collection of broken parts that each need a separate fix. It’s an interconnected system. And when one thing is off, it pulls other things off with it. Which means hacking one piece while ignoring the whole picture is like fixing one leg of a wobbly table and wondering why it still wobbles.

Chinese medicine has always understood this. The whole framework is built on getting your system to communicate with itself again. Customized herbal plans that work synergistically — not 15 isolated supplements competing for your body’s attention.

When the system works together, things start resolving that you didn’t even realize were connected.

That’s not magic. That’s just how your body was designed to work.
Save this for the next time you’re about to add another hack to the pile 📌
#HealthHacks #BiohackingMyth #ChineseMedicine #TCM #HolisticHealth

text:
Η Τρίτη 17 Φεβρουαρίου 2026 σηματοδοτεί μια ολοκαίνουργια χρονιά στο σεληνιακό ημερολόγιο, γνωστή και ως Κινεζική Πρωτοχρονιά ή Σεληνιακό Νέο Έτος.

Πάρτε τη σέλα σας και φορέστε τις μπότες ιππασίας σας — ήρθε η ώρα να μπείτε στη Χρονιά του Αλόγου!

Το Άλογο είναι το έβδομο ζωικό ζώδιο στο σεληνιακό ημερολόγιο. Το φετινό στοιχείο είναι η Φωτιά, η οποία σηματοδοτεί το πάθος και τον ενθουσιασμό και σχετίζεται ενεργειακά με την ενέργεια της Καρδιάς. Η Καρδιά είναι το κεντρικό σημείο επεξεργασίας για τη συνείδηση, τα συναισθήματα και το Πνεύμα (Shen) σας. Η Καρδιά ευδοκιμεί όταν είναι ειρηνική και ασκεί άνευ όρων αγάπη. Ολόκληρη η ύπαρξή σας βασίζεται στο ισορροπημένο Τσι της Καρδιάς. Θεωρούμενη ο βασιλιάς όλων των οργάνων, όλα τα άλλα όργανα θα θυσιάσουν ή θα δώσουν την ενέργειά τους για να βοηθήσουν την Καρδιά να διατηρήσει την ισορροπία της. Ενεργειακά, η Καρδιά σας λαμβάνει και μεταδίδει αμέτρητα μηνύματα μεταξύ των οργάνων. Εάν η Καρδιά σας δεν είναι ειρηνική, η λειτουργία της θα επηρεαστεί, κάτι που, με τη σειρά του, θα επηρεάσει το σύνολο.

Η κινεζική ιατρική μελετά τις αλληλεπιδράσεις. Η υγεία της καρδιάς εξαρτάται από την ισορροπία των πεπτικών σας οργάνων, του στομάχου και του ήπατος. Το στομάχι είναι το «παιδί» της καρδιάς. Εάν το στομάχι λειτουργεί καλά, η καρδιά είναι ευτυχισμένη ή επηρεάζεται λιγότερο. Η ενέργεια του στομάχου πρέπει να είναι σε ισορροπία για να εξισορροπηθεί η ενέργεια της καρδιάς. Το συκώτι είναι η «μητέρα» της καρδιάς. Μία από τις λειτουργίες του είναι να εξομαλύνει και να ρυθμίζει τα συναισθήματα. Όταν ένα άτομο βρίσκεται υπό συνεχή πίεση, η ενέργεια του ήπατος μειώνεται. Όταν αυτό το άγχος γίνεται χρόνιο, το συκώτι δεν μπορεί να υποστηρίξει σωστά την καρδιά.

Αυτό που το 2025 σας φάνηκε αργό, κολλημένο ή ασαφές είναι πιθανό να αποκτήσει δυναμική το 2026. Η Χρονιά του Πύρινου Αλόγου γενικά ευνοεί τη δράση, τη δημιουργικότητα και την κίνηση προς τα εμπρός. Με επίγνωση, πρακτικές γείωσης και στοχαστική αυτοφροντίδα, μπορεί να είναι μια δυναμική και γεμάτη ενέργεια χρονιά – μια χρονιά που θα σας βοηθήσει να ξεκινήσετε με αυτοπεποίθηση, σαφήνεια και ζωντάνια, χωρίς να εξαντληθείτε στην πορεία.

text:
Dein Kiefer lässt nicht los – egal, wie oft du „locker lassen“ denkst?

Dein Körper braucht oft mehr als einen Gedanken.

In der Übung im Reel legst du
🖐️ eine Hand auf den Bauch
🖐️ eine Hand sanft an den Kiefer

und lässt beides mit der Atmung weicher werden:
Bauch hebt & senkt sich,
Kiefer darf ein klein bisschen „einschmelzen“.

Es geht hier nicht darum, den Muskel mit Gewalt zu entspannen,
sondern deinem Nervensystem neue Signale zu geben:
	•	„Ich bin gerade sicher.“
	•	„Ich darf loslassen.“
	•	„Ich muss nicht beißen und festhalten.“

Menschen, die seit Jahren stark anspannen, werden nicht nach 30 Sekunden butterweich sein –
ihr System hat gelernt, immer auf Habacht zu sein.
Darum ist es normal, wenn du diese Übung immer wieder brauchst, bis sich etwas verändert.

🌿 In der TCM ist der Kiefer u. a. mit Magen- und Gallenblasen-Meridian verknüpft:
Verdauung von Nahrung – aber auch von Eindrücken, Ärger und „Herunterschlucken“.
Auch hier geht es weniger um einen einzelnen Muskel und mehr um das Gesamtmuster aus Stress, Emotionen und Spannung.

🧠 Wichtig: Das ist eine vereinfachte Erklärung und ersetzt keine individuelle Diagnose oder Behandlung. Jeder Körper reagiert anders.

💌 Wenn du merkst, dass du nicht nur einzelne Kiefer-Übungen,
sondern dein Nervensystem grundsätzlich anders organisieren möchtest:

In meinem Gruppenprogramm Resilience within arbeiten wir genau daran –
mit Nervensystem-Wissen, therapeutischem Yoga und TCM-Elementen,
damit dein Körper nicht mehr dauerhaft im Beiß- und Überlebensmodus festhängt.

post_owner.name: Dr. med. Daniela Victoria Grohmann
text:
As Medical Doctor & expert in Chinese medicine, this is where western medicine gets it all wrong about its Chinese counterpart 

1. Its not energy healing.
Qi — often translated as “vital energy” — refers to functional vitality: circulation, metabolism, defense and repair. Western medicine also relies on cellular energy production to sustain these processes.

2. It doesn’t reject science.
Many foundational concepts were described long before modern laboratory terminology existed. The observations came first. The molecular vocabulary came later.

3. It’s not mysticism.
Chinese Medicine is a systems-based clinical framework. It evaluates how physiological processes interact over time — rather than isolating symptoms.

4. The two systems don’t inherently conflict.
Much of the perceived tension lies in language and framework — not in the human physiology itself.
Integration doesn’t weaken science. It strengthens it.

🤎🤎🤎

Do you have PCOS?
 
In Western medicine, PCOS is often explained as a hormonal issue. 
 
But in Chinese Medicine, one of the most common root patterns behind PCOS is something called phlegm and blood stagnation stuck together.
 
Phlegm is considered a byproduct of weak digestion. 
 
It often develops from regularly consuming foods that are hard for the body to process—like iced drinks, soda, yogurt, ice cream, sweets, and fried foods. 
 
Over time, this pattern may show up as insulin resistance, high blood sugar, unexplained weight gain, and a constant feeling of heaviness and bloating.

Blood stagnation means the blood, especially in the uterus, is not flowing smoothly. 
 
This is when you may notice dark clots in your period, painful cramps, heavy bleeding, or periods that begin with dark brown spotting.
 
When phlegm and blood stagnation combine, it’s like a pipe clogged with thick mud—nothing flows properly. 
 
This can lead to late periods, skipped cycles, and disrupted ovulation.

If this imbalance remains untreated for a long time, it can generate heat in the body. 
 
That’s when you might see signs like higher stress levels, acne, excess hair growth, and even sticky stools.
 
Over time, deeper depletion can occur, leading to what Chinese Medicine calls kidney deficiency—when your foundational energy becomes weakened. 
 
This may show up as fertility challenges, hair loss, deep fatigue, and stubborn weight gain.
 
So PCOS is just a label. What truly matters is identifying and addressing the underlying imbalances in your body that are causing these symptoms in the first place.

Everyone repeats the statistic:
“70–80% of your immune system is in the gut.”

Yes, the gut is crucial.
But immunity isn’t stored in one place.
It’s coordinated across tissues.

Fascia — our connective tissue matrix — is biologically active.
It hosts immune cells.
It responds to mechanical stress.
It influences lymphatic flow and inflammatory signaling.

When fascia becomes restricted, communication changes.
And healing can slow down.

This is why fascia therapy isn’t “just massage.”
Mechanical stimulation affects cellular signaling.
Vibration regulates the nervous system.
Repair happens in parasympathetic mode.

And here’s what fascinates me most:

Traditional Chinese Medicine understood this systemic connection thousands of years ago.

TCM never separated organs from tissue, fluid from structure, or immunity from circulation.
Techniques like Tuina, Gua Sha, and lymphatic-style manual therapies were always about restoring flow — of Qi, blood, and fluids.

Modern fascia research is simply giving us new language for what ancient medicine already observed.

Your body is not a collection of isolated organs.
It’s an intelligent, communicating network.

If you’re curious about where modern immunology meets ancient medicine — stay here.

text:
Warum dein Nacken-Knoten immer wiederkommt – trotz Massage.

Der Punkt oben auf deiner Schulter ist selten „ein verspannter Muskel“.

In diesem Bereich treffen einige der kräftigsten Strukturen zusammen:

	•	oberer Trapezius
	•	Schulterblattheber/ Levator scapulae
	•	tiefere Nackenmuskeln
	•	Faszien, die Kopf, Hals und Schultergürtel „zusammenhalten“

Sie tragen dein Kopfgewicht, stabilisieren den Schultergürtel und fangen jede Armbewegung ab.

Wenn dein Nervensystem lange im Dauer-Alarm läuft, dreht es hier oft den Grundtonus hoch – das fühlt sich dann wie ein harter „Knoten“ unter den Fingern an.

Nur immer fester draufzudrücken erzählt deinem System schnell:

„Hier ist Gefahr“ – also spannt es noch mehr an.

Was ich bei mir selbst und in Sessions erlebe:

👉 Wenn ich den Punkt sanft halte oder mit MFR (Myo Fascial Release) bearbeite und gleichzeitig meinen Kopf & Nacken liebevoll, klein und langsam bewege,

	•	bekommt das Nervensystem neue, sichere Bewegungssignale
	•	die Faszie kann anders gleiten
	•	der Bereich muss weniger „Wache stehen“ – und wird oft schneller weich

🌿 Aus TCM-Sicht liegt dieser Spot im Verlauf des Gallenblasen-Meridians (und nahe am Blasen-Meridian) – einem Bereich, den man u. a. mit „Lasten auf den Schultern“, Entscheidungsdruck und gestautem Holz-Element verbindet.
Auch hier geht es nicht nur um den einen Punkt, sondern um das Muster dahinter.

🧠 Wichtig:
Das ist eine stark vereinfachte Erklärung. Jeder Körper reagiert anders.
Wiederkehrende oder starke Schmerzen gehören immer in die Hände von Ärzt:innen, Physio oder anderen Fachpersonen.
Alles, was ich hier teile, ist Ergänzung – keine Diagnose und keine Therapie.

⸻

In meinem kostenlosen Live-Webinar Sa. 21.02.2026 19-20 Uhr CET zeige ich dir, wie dauerhafte Spannung im Körper mit deinem Nervensystem zusammenhängt – und welche sanften, alltagstauglichen Tools du nutzen kannst, um aus dem Dauer-Alarm auszusteigen.

Customized herbal plans based on what’s actually happening with YOU. Not a generic stack from the internet.

text:
👉 Poznaj punkt, który rozluźnia twarz i wspiera żołądek.

👉 Żołądek 4 (ST4, Dicang) znajduje się przy kąciku ust, na przedłużeniu linii źrenicy. To ważny punkt meridianu żołądka, który przebiega przez twarz i ma bezpośredni wpływ na napięcia mięśniowe tej okolicy.

👉 W medycynie chińskiej twarz jest przedłużeniem pracy narządów. Gdy żołądek jest przeciążony, napięcie często pojawia się właśnie wokół ust.

👉 Masaż tego punktu jest szczególnie pomocny, gdy pojawia się:
• napięcie twarzy,
• zaciskanie ust,
• asymetria mięśni,
• uczucie ciężkiej twarzy,
• przeciążenie układu trawiennego.

👉 To także punkt często wykorzystywany w pracy terapeutycznej przy regeneracji mięśni twarzy.

👉 Jak masować punkt Żołądek 4?
Połóż opuszek palca na punkcie przy kąciku ust. Uciskaj delikatnie i wykonuj małe, powolne ruchy okrężne przez około 30–60 sekund. Oddychaj spokojnie. Nie używaj siły — twarz reaguje najlepiej na precyzję. Możesz masować oba punkty jednocześnie.

👉 Czasem rozluźnienie twarzy jest pierwszym sygnałem, że ciało zaczyna się uspokajać.

👉 5 dobrych rad:
1. Masuj punkt codziennie przez kilkadziesiąt sekund.
2. Najlepiej pracuj na rozluźnionej twarzy - nie zaciskaj zębów.
3. Połącz masaż ze spokojnym oddychaniem.
4. Jeśli punkt jest tkliwy, pracuj jeszcze delikatniej.
5. Regularność daje większy efekt niż mocny ucisk.

text:
This technique is actually a legitimate qigong practice for circulation and energy flow - but let’s be clear about what it actually does and doesn’t do.
What you’re seeing here is a specific tapping sequence targeting meridian endpoints in traditional Chinese medicine. The cupping motion creates vibration that practitioners believe stimulates energy channels connected to the heart and upper body.
In TCM theory, your hands contain the endpoints of major meridians - Pericardium, Heart, Lung, Large Intestine, Small Intestine, and Triple Burner channels. Tapping these areas is meant to promote qi flow, reduce stagnation, and support overall circulation.
The number nine has significance in many traditional practices - it’s considered a completion number, representing fullness and cycles. The cupping technique rather than flat palm creates deeper vibration into tissues without causing pain or surface trauma.
Here’s what this practice can actually do: improve circulation, reduce tension, support relaxation, potentially lower stress hormones, and create a meditative focus. Many people report feeling more energized and less tense after regular practice.
Here’s what it cannot do: clear arterial plaque, replace cardiac medication, treat diagnosed heart disease, or substitute for medical intervention when needed.

What pre should look like, or….what you think it should look like?! I don’t know….prep can be so unpredictable lol. 

A well-structured prep is smooth. Not easy (we would never be that lucky) but smooth. There’s a difference. Your weight trends down predictably. Your training performance is monitored. Cardio is added with intention, not panic. Food is adjusted strategically, not emotionally.

There will be phases where you have to push. That’s part of it. There are weeks where hunger is higher, where steps go up, where fatigue sets in. That’s prep. But those pushes should be controlled and calculated and not desperate reactions because you left things too late or go into prep in the best place possible.

If you’re in a good position, you should be able to bring refeeds in. You should be able to pull back slightly when needed. You should have room to manoeuvre. If you’re buried six weeks out with nowhere to go, that’s not “hardcore”, that’s unnecessary pushing.

The goal isn’t to suffer the most.
The goal is to present the best possible look on stage.

Outside of that NOBODY cares what it took to get on stage, how easy or how hard it was. 

Conditioned. Full. Balanced. Healthy enough to peak properly, if your body is running on fumes then trust me, bringing that back to “life” can be a challenge.

Prep is a performance phase, not a punishment phase. And if it’s structured properly, you don’t crawl to the stage, you arrive ready.

Suffering is for the ill, not competitive bodybuilders.

The stress-to-thyroid signaling pathway was.

Unterstützt die weitere Leitung entlang des Meridians und wird oft in Sequenz mit LR3 gearbeitet, um tiefer sitzende Spannung zu regulieren.

Jeden Punkt 30–60 Sekunden mit ruhigem, präzisem Druck stimulieren und dabei gleichmäßig weiteratmen. Beide Füße behandeln.

✨ How do you use a frozen Chinese soup pack? ✨

This is the question I get all the time since I started making these.

Good news: it’s SO easy. There are 2 ways I do it, but you can find others.

🍚 OPTION 1: Rice Cooker (my favourite) The ultimate set-it-and-forget-it method.
1️⃣ Take the frozen soup pack straight from the freezer
2️⃣ Drop it into your rice cooker
3️⃣ Fill water to the max line
4️⃣ Press “cook”
⏱ In about 1 hour, you’ll have a nourishing Chinese soup ready to serve.

Honestly… if your child knows how to use a rice cooker, you’re good 😄

🔥 OPTION 2: Stove Top
1️⃣ Add the frozen soup pack to a pot
2️⃣ Add 7 cups of water
3️⃣ Bring to a boil
4️⃣ Reduce to medium heat and simmer for 1 hour (or use a thermal pot)

(Pro tip: set a timer so you don’t forget!)

🌿 Make it your own, you can always add:
• Fresh vegetables
• Extra herbs
• Salt to taste

💛 The whole point of these soup packs? To make soup making easy, convenient, and accessible — even on busy days. If you want to learn how I make these frozen soup packs, check the earlier videos.

text:
آلام دورتكِ ليست طبيعية… هذا ما يقوله الطب الصيني

فـالطب الصيني التقليدي لا يعتبر آلام الدورة الشهرية أمرًا طبيعيًا يجب التعايش معه، بل إشارة واضحة إلى خلل داخل الجسم. لذلك يركّز العلاج على فهم السبب الحقيقي للألم—هل هو انسداد، برودة، أو نقص في الطاقة—ثم معالجة الجذور بلطف وعمق بدل الاكتفاء بتسكين الأعراض.
بروتوكول الطب الصيني التقليدي وبشكل مبسّط، هذا هو الإطار العلاجي المتبع:

أولًا: إذا كان الألم ناتجًا عن انسداد (ركود طاقة أو دم)
الهدف هنا هو تحريك التدفق وإزالة الركود.

* تدفئة الجسم وتجنّب البرودة (مشروبات باردة، أطعمة نيئة، تعرّض أسفل الجسم للبرد)
* استخدام الكمادات الدافئة على أسفل البطن وأسفل الظهر
* نقع القدمين بماء دافئ، خاصة قبل الدورة
* تقليل التوتر لأن الضغط النفسي يسبب ركود طاقة الكبد

ثانيًا: إذا كان الألم ناتجًا عن نقص الدفء أو الطاقة (نقص اليانغ) الهدف هو تغذية الجسم وتدفئة الرحم.

* التركيز على أطعمة دافئة ومطبوخة (شوربات، مرق، جذور)
* تجنّب الصيام القاسي أو تقليل السعرات بشكل مفرط
* النوم الكافي ودعم الجسم قبل وأثناء الدورة
* استخدام الحرارة بانتظام لأن الدفء يخفف الألم بوضوح
* الأعشاب هنا تُستخدم لدعم الطاقة، الدم، ودفء الرحم

ثالثًا: دعم نمط الحياة (أساس البروتوكول)

* تنظيم النوم وتقليل السهر
* تخفيف التوتر العاطفي (لأن الكبد مرتبط مباشرة بالدورة في الطب الصيني)
* حركة لطيفة مثل المشي أو التمدد بدل التمارين العنيفة أثناء الألم
* عدم تجاهل الإرهاق المزمن لأنه يضعف طاقة الجسم

رابعًا: إستخدام أعشاب من الطب الصيني التقليدي بحسب سبب ألم الدورة:

تشاي هو (Chai Hu) يساعد على تخفيف آلام الدورة المرتبطة بالتوتر وركود الطاقة.
باي شاو (Bai Shao) يخفف التشنجات ويغذي الدم، ومفيد عند التعب وضعف الجسم.
غان جيانغ (Gan Jiang) وهو الزنجبيل المجفف، يدفئ الرحم ويخفف الألم الناتج عن البرودة.

 🍀 في الطب الصيني العلاج لا يبدأ بمسكّن، بل بإعادة الانسياب، التوازن، والدفء للجسم — وعندها يخف الألم من جذوره، لا مؤقتًا فقط.

✔ Supports lymphatic drainage

1. Yintang (Third Eye Point)
Start with a gentle press between the eyebrows.
Helps calm the mind, reduce stress-related pigmentation, and improve overall facial circulation.

2. UB2 (Bladder Meridian 2)
Located at the inner corner of the eyebrows.
Use your knuckle or fingertip to stimulate blood flow and reduce under-eye darkness.

3. SJ23 (Triple Burner 23)
Brush gently towards the outer end of the eyebrow.
Helps reduce puffiness, eye strain, and supports lymphatic movement.

4. ST2 (Stomach Meridian 2)
Press gently below the eyes to activate circulation and reduce fluid buildup.

5. Taiyang (Temple Point)
A powerful detox point that refreshes the eyes, reduces headaches, and relieves tension stored around the temples.

🌸 Why This Works

Dark circles and eye bags are often caused by poor circulation, lymph congestion, stress, dehydration, and screen fatigue. Acupressure improves prana/qi flow, helping the body heal from within rather than masking the problem externally.

🌿 How Often to Practice

🕒 Once or twice daily
Best done morning (to reduce puffiness) and night (to relax eye muscles)

True beauty is not created by products alone.

text:
—
Ever notice how you’re “doing all the right things” — daily salads, cold smoothies, iced water — yet you’re still bloated, tired, and craving sugar by 3pm?

From a Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) perspective, this often points to something called Spleen Qi deficiency — and no, it has nothing to do with your anatomical spleen.

In TCM, the Spleen is responsible for digestion, energy production, and nutrient extraction. Think of it as your body’s internal digestive fire. When it’s strong, food is efficiently broken down into energy. When it’s weak, food just… sits.

Here’s where modern “clean eating” can backfire:

Raw foods require more digestive energy
Raw vegetables, salads, and smoothies are cooling by nature. Your body has to work harder to warm them up before digestion can even begin. If your digestive system is already tired, this extra demand can lead to bloating, gas, loose stools, and fatigue.

Iced water puts the fire out
Drinking cold or iced beverages with meals is like pouring water on a campfire. It slows digestion, dilutes digestive enzymes, and weakens the body’s ability to properly transform food into usable energy.

Why this leads to fatigue
When food isn’t fully digested, your body doesn’t get the energy it needs — even if you’re eating “healthy.” This shows up as low energy, brain fog, heaviness after meals, and sugar or caffeine cravings.

Common signs of Spleen Qi deficiency include:
• Bloating after eating
• Fatigue or heaviness in the body
• Loose stools or irregular digestion
• Brain fog
• Cravings for sweets
• Feeling worse after raw or cold foods

The solution isn’t cutting out vegetables — it’s supporting digestion.

What helps instead:
• Warm, cooked foods (soups, stews, roasted veggies)
• Room-temperature or warm beverages with meals
• Gentle spices like ginger or cinnamon
• Regular meal timing
• Eating in a relaxed state (yes, stress matters)

Connecting 2 medicines to create 1 holistic system 🤝
I am a Medical Doctor & Expert in Chinese Medicine, connecting both medicine systems and translating one into the other. 
What we find is that they use different models to explain the same physiological processes. 

1. Qi → cellular energy & repair 
(both describe how well the body generates energy for health, daily activity & healing)

2. Dampness → low grade inflammation
Dampness forms when digestion, fluid metabolism or movement are impaired — often from stress, ultra-processed foods or inactivity. Western medicine describes this state as persistent low-grade inflammation.

3. Shen → body-mind stress regulation
Shen disturbance comes from emotional overload. In Western medicine, chronic stress alters brain–nervous–immune communication, cortisol and inflammation.

4. Blood deficiency → nourishment impaired 
blood deficiency comes from poor digestion, stress, blood loss or under-eating. Western medicine explains this as insufficient delivery of oxygen and nutrients to tissues.

5. Yin & Yang → Imbalance activation and recovery
In TCM, imbalance arises when stimulation (work, exercise, stress) chronically outweighs rest and nourishment. Western medicine describes this as prolonged nervous system activation with insufficient recovery, disrupting hormones, sleep and immune regulation.

A licitação da limpeza urbana e operação do aterro municipal, prevista para acontecer no próximo dia 13, foi barrada e pode prolongar o pesadelo da Quebec Ambiental por mais um ano em Anápolis.

O Tribunal de Contas dos Municípios de Goiás (TCM-GO) manteve a suspensão do edital após identificar que não foram cumpridas as determinações técnicas feitas anteriormente pelo órgão.

A decisão frustra a expectativa de encontrar um sucessor para a Quebec, empresa que opera o segmento em Anápolis atualmente e acumula histórico de reclamações envolvendo o serviço de coleta e limpeza urbana no município.

Com isso, o cenário vai se desenhando para que a atuação aquém da Quebec se prolongue em mais um termo aditivo, que seria a 11º extensão emergencial de um vínculo que se estende desde 2020 e acumula valor próximo de R$ 500 milhões.

Ao analisar o caso, o TCM destacou que persistem falhas materiais no edital, o que torna impossível a continuidade da licitação neste momento.

A Corte foi explícita ao afirmar que as determinações técnicas expedidas anteriormente não foram integralmente cumpridas pela Prefeitura, caracterizando descumprimento material das decisões proferidas.

Embora a paralisação seja formalmente atribuída ao TCM, os acórdãos deixam claro que o impasse decorre da manutenção de um edital sem o saneamento completo dos vícios já apontados.

🫖 Niin ihana aihe ja mulle osa mun arkeani!

Moni on kysynyt multa viime aikoina, miksi juon aamulla ja pitkin päivää lämmintä vettä. 
Ensiksikin, mä rakastan sen makua, mielestäni se on jotenkin pehmeämpään.

Tämä ei ole trendi, vaan tämän on osa kiinalaisen lääketieteen (TCM) perusajattelua, jota olen oppinut mestareiltani ja opettajiltani vuosien varrella.

🔥 Kehon lämpötila ja ruoansulatus

TCM:n mukaan kehon ruoansulatus toimii parhaiten kehonlämmössä.
Kun juomme kylmää vettä, keho joutuu ensin lämmittämään nesteen, ennen kuin se voi käyttää sitä. Tämä vie energiaa erityisesti pernalta ja vatsalta, jotka vastaavat ravinnon muuttamisesta energiaksi.

Lämmin tai keitetty vesi:
	•	tukee suoliston luonnollista liikettä
	•	on lempeä vatsalle
	•	auttaa kehoa heräämään aamulla ilman shokkia

🌿 Suolisto ja kuona-aineet

TCM:ssä sanotaan, että lämmin vesi auttaa liikettä.
Aamulla juotu lämmin vesi voi:
	•	käynnistää suoliston toimintaa
	•	auttaa kuona-aineiden poistumista
	•	tukea säännöllisyyttä ilman pakottamista

🩸 Vaikutus qi:hin ja verenkiertoon

Lämpö avaa, kylmä supistaa.
Lämmin vesi tukee qi:n ja veren virtausta, kun taas kylmä voi aiheuttaa:
	•	jännitystä
	•	tukkoisuutta
	•	kylmyyden tunnetta kehossa

Tämä on yksi syy, miksi TCM:ssä suositellaan lämpimiä juomia erityisesti:
	•	naisille
	•	kylmyyteen taipuvaisille
	•	stressaantuneille
	•	talviaikaan

🚰 Miksi ei suoraan kuumaa vettä hanasta?

Tärkeä huomio:
TCM:n ja nykysuositusten mukaan kuumaa vettä ei suositella juotavaksi suoraan hanasta, mm.:
	•	kuuma vesi voi irrottaa putkistoista 
  epäpuhtauksia
	•	maku ja laatu eivät ole optimaalisia

👉 Siksi paras vaihtoehto on keitetty ja hieman jäähtynyt vesi tai vedenkeittimellä lämmitetty vesi.

🌸 Lempeä tapa hoitaa kehoa

TCM ei perustu ääripäihin, vaan kuuntelemiseen ja tasapainoon.
Lämmin vesi ei ole “pakko”, vaan kutsu:
Kuunnella kehoa, tukea sitä lempeästi ja
vähentää turhaa kuormitusta.

Itse huomaan eron erityisesti vatsassa, energiassa ja kehon rauhassa.

Think of it as a friendly reminder that even herbal remedies have a personality.

The big news? Most popular products are fine. The rule mainly targets those long‑dead “zombie” formulas that haven’t been produced in years. Companies are already updating their labels, and the cost is way lower than it used to be – a few thousand yuan instead of hundreds of thousands. It’s a win‑win: clearer information for everyone, and no mass delistings.

It’s also a push toward transparency. Beijing wants to modernize the sector, so we’re seeing more real‑world studies and post‑market evaluations. The industry is stepping up, and the changes are happening in a few months, not decades.

Bottom line: the era of “unclear” is ending, but the market’s still thriving. A little more clarity, a lot more confidence.

Not all bread is created equal 🍞🌿
TCM-approved for organ support ✅

Ingredients 🥣
• 3 cups flour 🌾
• 2 tbsp flaxseed 🌱
• 2 tbsp black sesame ⚫️
• 1 egg 🥚
• 1 tbsp yeast 🍶
• 1 tsp honey 🍯
• Warm water 💧 (as needed)

**I forgot to add salt, you can add 1/4 teaspoon **

Instructions 👩🏽‍🍳
Mix warm water 💧 with honey 🍯 and yeast 🍶.
Let it foam 5–10 minutes ⏳.

In a bowl, combine flour 🌾, flaxseed 🌱, and black sesame 

Add the egg 🥚 and yeast mixture,
then mix to form a dough 🤲🏽.

Knead 3–5 minutes until smooth ✨.

Let rise about 2 hours ⏱️, until doubled.

Shape into a loaf or two small ones 
then let rise another 30 minutes ⏳

Bake at 375°F 🔥 for 25–30 minutes

Cool completely, before slicing 😋

👉🏻Hafıza sorunları birçok nedenle ortaya çıkabilir. Batı tıbbına göre unutkanlık; genetik yatkınlık, stres, depresyon, yetersiz uyku, tiroit dengesizlikleri, bazı ilaçlar, susuz kalma ve besin değeri düşük beslenme ile ilişkilidir — ve bu faktörlerin tamamı hafızayı etkileyebilir.

• Dalak (Spleen): Kısa süreli hafıza, analiz, odaklanma, ders çalışma ve konsantrasyonla ilişkilidir. Yanlış beslenme ve aşırı zihinsel kaygı ile zayıflar. Dalak’ın zihinsel yönü “Yi” olarak adlandırılır ve fikir/niyet anlamına gelir, düşünme sekli, algılamadır.

Across ancient healing systems like Ayurveda, Traditional Chinese Medicine, Mediterranean traditions optimal health always came back to the same principle:

👉 Balance the environment with the opposite quality.
Cold outside: introduce warmth inside.
Heat outside: introduce cooling support.

When it’s cold, the body benefits from warm, cooked, easy-to-digest foods that support digestion first so immunity can follow.

That’s why this soup works:

🎃 Pumpkin + Sweet Potato
Rich in beta-carotene (vitamin A) supports immune cells, gut and respiratory barriers.

🌿 Thyme
Contains thymol + flavonoids traditionally used to support respiratory and immune health.

🧄 Garlic + Onion
High in sulfur compounds support immune signaling, gut health, and inflammatory balance.

🟡 Turmeric + Black Pepper
Curcuminoids + piperine support inflammatory regulation and nutrient absorption.

🌱 Fresh Ginger Root
Supports circulation, digestion, and internal warmth reducing digestive load in cold conditions.

🧈 Healthy fats
Essential for absorbing fat-soluble compounds like vitamin A and curcumin.

✨ The takeaway:
This isn’t seasonal nostalgia it’s biological balance.
Warm foods help restore resilience when the environment is cold.

Not one-size-fits-all.
Best for cold, stressed, or depleted systems timing and bio-individuality always matter.

3 Acupressure Points to Brighten Tired Eyes and Lift Your Brows Naturally
When your eyes feel puffy, heavy, or dull from lack of sleep, ptosis,screen time, or allergies, try this quick facial acupressure routine to refresh your appearance and boost circulation. This method, from traditional Chinese medicine supports eye care and fits into any natural beauty routine, especially when you’re avoiding injectables or just want something quick and effective.

1. GB2
This point is at the outer end of the eyebrow. Gently press into the small dip in the bone and massage with light pressure. It helps release facial tension and can reduce puffiness around the eyes.

2. YUYAO
Found in the center of the eyebrow, right above the pupil. Press and massage gently to relieve strain, calm the facial muscles, and support relaxation. This one’s especially helpful after hours of screen time or when you feel mentally foggy.

3. GB14
Located one finger above YUYAO on the forehead. Find the shallow dip and massage slowly. It can lift the brow area and support sinus drainage. This point is often used to refresh tired, heavy eyes and subtly lift the face without needles or tools.

This technique is part of traditional acupressure and can be done anytime. It’s ideal when you can’t get a facial, haven’t slept well, or just want to give your face a natural, no-tox refresh. Take a deep breath as you massage each point for 30 seconds.

Whether you’re into holistic wellness, natural beauty remedies, or looking for no Botox alternatives, this is a simple yet powerful way to take care of your face with your own hands.

Did you know those little white seeds floating in Chinese soups are actually a traditional herbal ingredient used for over 1,000 years? These are apricot kernels (南北杏 in Cantonese)! There are 2 types available:

🌿 North Apricot Kernel (北 meaning North)
• Smaller, flatter, heart-shaped
• Bitter, warming, more medicinal
• Used for stronger coughs & wheezing
• Always pre-processed for safety

🌿 South Apricot Kernel (南 meaning South)
• Plumper, oval, food-grade safe
• Sweet, neutral & nourishing
• Great for dry coughs & moistening lungs/intestines

In TCM, both support:
🔻Lungs & Large Intestine
🔻Cough relief & breathing (asthma relief)
🔻Gentle bowel movement

🍲 I usually use a mix in soups & teas (more South than North — about 1:4 ratio)

⚠️ Avoid if you have:
• Excess dampness or phlegm
• Weak digestion/bloating
• Acute diarrhea
• Pregnancy or babies (especially North kernels)

You’ll often find South kernels in almond tea, snow fungus desserts, and nourishing soups 🤍

✨ Small but powerful, the apricot kernels in soups and teas ✨

Did you know those little white seeds floating in Chinese soups are actually a traditional herbal ingredient used for over 1,000 years? These are apricot kernels (南北杏 in Cantonese)! There are 2 types available:

🌿 North Apricot Kernel (北 meaning North)
• Smaller, flatter, heart-shaped
• Bitter, warming, more medicinal
• Used for stronger coughs & wheezing
• Always pre-processed for safety

🌿 South Apricot Kernel (南 meaning South)
• Plumper, oval, food-grade safe
• Sweet, neutral & nourishing
• Great for dry coughs & moistening lungs/intestines

In TCM, both support:
🔻Lungs & Large Intestine
🔻Cough relief & breathing (asthma relief)
🔻Gentle bowel movement

🍲 I usually use a mix in soups & teas (more South than North — about 1:4 ratio)

⚠️ Avoid if you have:
• Excess dampness or phlegm
• Weak digestion/bloating
• Acute diarrhea
• Pregnancy or babies (especially North kernels)

You’ll often find South kernels in almond tea, snow fungus desserts, and nourishing soups 🤍

Have you used apricot kernels before? Let me know in the comments!

text:
If this cold weather is hitting you hard, this is your sign to make this ginger lemonade immunity tea. ☕️

This tea tastes amazing – cozy, lightly spicy, and bright from the lemon! 

Ingredients:

• 1 small knob of fresh ginger, sliced
• 1 lemon (½ sliced for the pot, ½ reserved for later)
• 1–2 star anise pods
• Optional: a pinch of cinnamon powder
• Raw honey (add to taste)

How to make it:

Add the ginger, lemon slices, star anise (and cinnamon if using) to about 10 oz of water. Bring to a boil and simmer for at least 10 minutes. Longer simmer = more flavor.

Strain into a mug. Let it cool slightly, then add the remaining fresh lemon juice and raw honey to taste. 

Let us know if you end up making this! 🙌

Happy Laba festival 

Het Laba Festival valt op de achtste dag van de twaalfde maanmaand.

In China is dit een bewust moment in het jaar om stil te staan bij gezondheid en veerkracht.

Op deze dag wordt in veel regio’s Laba-congee gegeten. Niet als feestmaal, maar als iets functioneels: eten dat je lichaam helpt herstellen na een lange winterperiode. De congee bestaat uit meerdere ingrediënten zoals rijst, gierst, verschillende bonen en soms kruiden en staat daarom ook bekend als Eight-Treasure of Five-Flavor congee.

Volgens de Chinese geneeskunde ondersteunt deze congee de vijf Zang-organen, helpt ze het lichaam weer op krachten te komen en verkleint ze de kans dat je het nieuwe jaar begint met klachten of terugkerende vermoeidheid.

De traditie gaat terug tot de Song-dynastie. Rode bonen werden toegevoegd met het idee om “slechte geesten” te verjagen. In praktische zin betekent dat: het lichaam helpen loslaten wat belastend is en weer meer balans creëren.

Wanneer je deze congee regelmatig eet, wordt ze gezien als ondersteuning voor het Bloed, het Hart en je algehele vitaliteit. 
Warm, voedend en goed verteerbaar. Een eenvoudige manier om je lichaam te geven wat het in deze fase nodig heeft.

Laba herinnert je eraan dat gezondheid niet begint bij forceren of verbeteren, maar bij aanvullen. Zorgen dat je basis sterk genoeg is, zodat je met meer energie en stabiliteit het nieuwe jaar in gaat.

Como oncologista, é fundamental reforçar que medidas regulatórias como essa não são alarmismo, mas sim decisões baseadas no princípio da precaução, amplamente utilizado na saúde. Já que há evidência científica de dano em ratos de laboratório, a prioridade deve ser sempre proteger a população, mesmo antes de danos maiores serem observados em humanos.

É de extrema importância questionar a segurança de produtos de uso contínuo, buscar informação de qualidade e valorizar decisões que colocam a saúde acima de tendências estéticas.

text:
Stop poppin cough drops if you have a dry cough that won’t go away after being sick— try making BAE-SUK (배숙): a traditional Korean steamed pear cough & cold remedy 🍐 

Added a little twist to this recipe by adding Schisandra berries (a really powerful, naturally medicinal berry often used in TCM) and Celtic sea salt for even better cough relief + minerals.

I got mine from Hmart but you can also find the dried versions on Amazon— or just replace it with goji berries.

Because ✨food is medicine✨

RECIPE:
- 1 lb Korean pear (or a large Bartlett or Bosc pear)
- 2 tbs honey
- 3-4 slices of ginger, grated or chopped
- 1/4 tsp cinnamon powder
- 1/2 tsp Schisandra berries (or goji)
- 2 jujubes, pits removed 
- pinch of Celtic sea salt or Himalayan pink salt

1. Rinse the pear and pat dry. Make a lid by slicing 1 inch off the top.
2. Scoop out the core & seeds, leaving about 1 inch of room around the sides 
3. Fill the core with the honey & other ingredients 
4. Put the sliced “lid” back on to the pear and steam the pear for 30 min over medium-high heat.
5. Let the pear cool for 5-10 min, then remove the Schisandra berries and larger ginger pieces.
6. Serve warm and enjoy the pear and the remaining juice!
