Ep. 5: sprained ankle? 🦶😩 [read💌⤵️]

I’m Chee Hee, a Chinese Medicine student from Malaysia 🇲🇾 and I’m graduating this year! Before that, I want to take you on this journey with me and learn different acupuncture points in your body that you can massage yourself for specific conditions 💛 so join me and follow along for more.

In this fifth episode, I introduced the acupuncture point YangChi (SJ4), a favorite point for ankle sprains. In Chinese Medicine, reflective zones are areas on a body that are connected to other areas. By treating a reflective zone, the affected area will also feel relieved. Ankle ligamentous sprain injury is the most common single type of acute sport trauma. So share this to your friends. You never know who might need this💛

SJ4, also known as YangChi, is another effective acupressure point for relieving pain from ankle injuries. Move the wrist in a relaxed way so that the joint space is more visible. Yangchi SJ4 is located in the depression where your fingers are joint at the bone, between your ring finger and pinky finger.

YangChi is known to relax tendons and help with pain in the neck, arms, and shoulders. It also benefits the ears and it is indicated for symptoms such as tinnitus, deafness and ear pain. 

Massage gently in small circles. Do this for 1-3 minutes while gently rotating your ankle and moving it side to side. You should have a deep aching feeling on your wrist and a feeling of relaxation and relief. Let me know if it works 🥰

Note: the point may shift slightly from person to person, but there should be a soreness in the wrist area. If it isn’t sore, you’re not doing it right. Search your wrist area for a sore point and massage that point instead.

PS: you need to rest your ankle during this time, elevate your ankle, and ice it during the first 24 hours. Make sure to go through proper rehab and regain the strength in your ankles. Acupuncture is a great treatment for ankle sprains too, so make sure to find a local acupuncturist for a speedy recovery.

text:
Herbal medicine has been a cornerstone of human health & spiritual practice across cultures for millennia. Before the advent of modern science, societies around the world recognized that plants possess both healing & energetic properties. Indigenous peoples cultivated gardens & gathered wild herbs with an understanding of plant cycles, seasonal rhythms & the interconnectedness of all living beings, intuitively linking wellness to the environment & spiritual balance. In African traditions, plants were incorporated into rituals, ancestral work & folk healing, combining empirical knowledge of medicinal properties with an awareness of the spiritual forces inherent in nature. Similarly, Chinese medicine developed sophisticated frameworks such as yin & yang, qi & hot-cold energetics to explain the effects of herbs on the body, providing a systematized approach to herbal therapy that could predict outcomes long before modern pharmacology confirmed them.

Across these diverse traditions, there was a shared recognition that plants are more than passive remedies. They were seen as active participants in healing whether through physical restoration, spiritual protection, or energetic balancing. Communities observed, experimented & passed down this knowledge orally or through ritual practice, creating complex systems that combined practical medicine, spiritual insight & ethical stewardship of the natural world. Remarkably, these systems often anticipated discoveries that modern science would later validate. Active compounds, anti-inflammatory properties & psychoactive effects in certain herbs were understood intuitively as part of holistic health practices, even if the biochemical mechanisms were unknown.

Double-Boiled Chicken Soup with Ginger & Red Dates | Nourishing TCM Recipe for Energy & Digestion

Warm, nourishing and incredibly easy to make! This double-boiled chicken soup with ginger and dried red dates is a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) recipe for supporting energy, digestion, circulation, and postpartum recovery. This recipe is simple, comforting, and deeply nourishing for the body, especially when you feel cold, tired, depleted or run down.

In TCM, this soup is:
✨ warm in nature - if you’re feeling cold, cold stomach, chills
✨ tonifies qi and blood - if you’re feeling low in energy, fatigue
✨ supports digestion and circulation
✨ gently warms the spleen and stomach
✨ comforting for fatigue, cold body, low appetite and low energy - if you’re feeling busy, exhausted
✨ perfect for postpartum, post surgery, and post period

Dried red dates nourish blood and qi, while fresh ginger gently warms the digestion without being overly hot. Chicken breast provides lean protein and strength. Together, they create a deeply soothing, restorative soup.

🍲 Ingredients, serves 4;
500 g of chicken breast (keep whole)
10 whole dried red dates (pitted)
10 slices of fresh ginger
7-8 cups of cold water (average is 2 cups per bowl if you’re making individual portions)

Honestly, I sometimes eyeball this soup as well and use what I feel like!

🔥 Why Double-Boiled?
Double boiling is a traditional method that keeps the flavour and nutrients pure, without clouding the broth. It results in a clean, clear, aromatic soup that feels light on the body yet deeply comforting.

⚠️ Avoid, if you have:
❌ Heat signs (red face, irritability, dry mouth, mouth or tongue ulcers)
❌ Damp-heat acne
❌ Very hot, inflamed conditions
You can reduce ginger and dates, and use ginger skin instead of ginger flesh or add winter melon.

🦷 Was die Zähne zeigen:
Tonnenzähne = Lueshinweis
Zahnschmerz bei starkem Druck, kalt und sehr heiss = Zahnwurzelentzündung (Pulpitis)
Zahnschmerz bei Druck und Klopfen und heiss, nicht aber bei Kälte = Granulom

👄 Was der Mund uns sagen kann:
Brauner Mundhof = Darmerkrankungen
Blasser, schmaler Mund bei Frauen = Östrogenmangel, Dysmenorrhoe
Lippencyanose = Herzinsuffizienz

👀 Was die Schläfen sagen:
Stark vorstehende, geschlängelte Schläfenarterie und rotes Gesicht = Arteriitis temporalis, essentieller Hochdruck, Nierenbelastung
Mit blassem Gesicht = Renaler Hochdruck, Arterioskle-rose, Cerebralsklerose
Mit Cyanose = Obere Hohlvenenstauung

ℹ️ Zur Information: dieses Wissen habe ich mir selbstverständlich nicht ausgedacht, sondern es entstammt der Pathophysiognomie:
Das ist das Lesen von sichtbaren Zeichen, die zeigen, wo im System gerade etwas blockiert, überfordert oder aus dem Gleichgewicht geraten ist.

Wenn du genaueres dazu erfahren möchtest empfehle ich dir das Buch „Krankheiten aus dem Gesicht erkennen“ von Kurt Tepperwein.

Ep. 4: period pain😣🤦‍♀️[i gotchu💌⤵️]

I’m Chee Hee, a Chinese Medicine student and I’m graduating this year! Before that, I want to take you on this journey with me and learn different acupuncture points in your body that you can massage yourself for specific conditions 💛 so join me and follow along for more.

In this fourth episode, I introduced the acupuncture point SanYinJiao (SP6), a favorite point for period pain(dysmenorrhea/menstrual cramps). Reports on the incidence of primary dysmenorrhea vary considerably, ranging from 20% to up to 90% of menstruating females. So share this to your friends. You never know who might need this💛

Acupressure is a traditional Chinese healing technique that involves applying pressure to specific points on the body to promote relaxation, relieve pain, and [improve overall healt](https://www.healthfab.in/blogs/lifestyle/ways-to-improve-mental-health-during-periods)h.

SP6, also known as Sanyinjiao, is another effective acupressure point for relieving period pain. It is located on the inner side of the calf, three finger widths above the ankle bone and between the two tendons. Sanyinjiao is known to regulate the menstrual cycle and is often used to relieve menstrual cramps, lower back pain, and irregular periods. 

Massage gently in small circles. Do this for 1-3 minutes. You can do it yourself or do it for someone else. You should have a deep aching feeling and a feeling of relaxation and relief. Let me know if it works 🥰

Note: Do not use SP6 during pregnancy! When there was period problems such as dysmenorrhea, or unusual color and cycle of menstruation, it has the best therapeutic effect when massaging Sanyinjiao point a week before the menstrual period.

Evidence Based Study: There are many articles published about this acupuncture point and I think this is one that’s pretty interesting: “Effect of acupressure at the Sanyinjiao point on primary dysmenorrhea: A randomized controlled trial”

text:
Lunge 7 - der Erkältungspunkt wirkt schleimlösend und reguliert die Wasserwege im Körper. 

Er liegt auf der Unterarmkante, am Griffelvorsatz - ca 2 fingerbreit von der Handgelenksfalte.

Am einfachsten findest du Lunge 7 wenn du Daumen und Zeigefinger beider Hände ineinander verschränkst. Dort wo die Spitze des Zeigefingers auf der Armkante landet, ist zwischen den Sehnen eine kleine Mulde. Dort liegt der Punkt.

Lu 7 ist der Erkältungspunkt schlechthin. Er öffnet die oberen und unteren Wasserwege und wirkt schleimlösend. Daher hilft er bei Heuschnupfen oder verstopfter Nase und wird bei Wasserablagerungen und Ödemen angewandt.

Lunge 7 ist besonders, da er der Schlüsselpunkt des Konzeptionsgefäßes ist, das an der Körpervorderseite verläuft. Als Meisterpunkt reguliert er alle Yin-Leitbahnen. Er wird gerne bei Schwangerschaftsbeschwerden verwendet, und hilft grundsätzlich bei allen Frauenthemen, wie Wechseljahre oder Menstruation.

Psychologisch wirkt Lunge 7 auch bei Trauer, denn Weinen ist der stimmliche Ausdruck der Lunge. Wenn bei Kummer oder einem schweren Verlust das Weinen unterdrückt wird, hilft LU 7 Gefühle zu befreien und Blockaden zu lösen.

Du kannst den Punkt auf beiden Seiten 2-3 Mal am Tag bis zu einer Minute sanft drücken.

text:
Duże skrzepy podczas menstruacji to znak, że coś się dzieje w organizmie. Medycyna zachodnia i TCM tłumaczą to różnie, ale obie mają rację.

W medycynie chińskiej praktyk powie: "to zimno w macicy powoduje stagnację krwi". W gabinecie ginekologicznym usłyszysz: "może to być adenomioza, mięśniaki lub zaburzenia hormonalne". Dwie narracje, ten sam problem.

Fizjologia jest prosta. Krew menstruacyjna zawiera naturalnie antykoagulanty zapobiegające krzepnięciu. Kiedy krwawienie jest ciężkie lub mechanizmy przeciążone, powstają skrzepy. TCM patrzy na to przez pryzmat "zimna kongelującego krew" - nie chodzi o dosłowną temperaturę, ale o spowolnienie mikrocyrkulacji. Vazokonstrykcja z medycyny zachodniej to ten sam kurcz naczyń, o którym mówi TCM. Tylko używamy innych słów.

Co łączy obie tradycje? Ciepło pomaga. Poduszka cieplna przy 40-42°C rozluźnia mięsień gładki macicy i jest to udokumentowany efekt analgetyczny. W TCM osiąga się to moksybucją na punkty CV4 czy SP6. Mechanizm podobny, technika inna.

Badania Cochrane (PMID: 27087494) potwierdzają skuteczność akupunktury w dysmenorrhei przez modulację przewodnictwa bólowego i uwalnianie endorfin. TCM powiedziałby: "usuwa stazę i aktywuje przepływ Qi". Różne języki, podobny rezultat 🎯

Praktycznie wygląda to tak: jeśli masz skrzepy większe niż 2,5 cm, najpierw ginekolog i USG. Wykluczamy patologie. Potem budujesz strategię: dieta antyinflamacyjna z omega-3, magnezem, imbirem. Termoterapia w czasie menstruacji. Jeśli potrzebujesz więcej, dodajesz akupunkturę albo NSAIDs.

TCM zaleca unikanie zimnych napojów podczas menstruacji. Fizjologicznie brak twardych dowodów na bezpośredni wpływ na macicę, ale ciepłe napoje przynoszą komfort i relaksację. Czasem efekt psychosomatyczny jest równie realny jak farmakologiczny.

Nie chodzi o wybieranie stron. Medycyna zachodnia daje diagnostykę obrazową i farmakologię. TCM oferuje akupunkturę, dietetykę energetyczną, spojrzenie całościowe. Najlepsze rezultaty daje połączenie, nie wykluczanie.

Masz skrzepy? Co robiłaś do tej pory?

post_owner.name: Biohacking | Zdrowie + Nauka 🔬
text:
Tysiące lat medycyny chińskiej mówiły o "ogniu wewnętrznym", który oczyszcza i harmonizuje organizm. Współczesna farmakologia odkryła, co dokładnie stało za tą metaforą.

W Tradycyjnej Medycynie Chińskiej imbir to środek o ciepłej naturze, który "ociepla meridian śledziony, rozprasza zimno i harmonizuje przepływ Qi". Nauka pokazuje mechanizmy: gingerole i shogaole hamują szlak zapalny NF-κB, zmniejszając poziomy białka CRP oraz cytokinę TNF-α (PMID: 32763761). Metaanaliza 16 badań klinicznych potwierdza znaczącą redukcję markerów zapalnych u osób regularnie stosujących imbir.

Fascynujące jest, jak różne formy imbiru odpowiadają różnym mechanizmom. Świeży zawiera więcej gingeroli, działa łagodniej na układ trawienny. Podczas suszenia gingerole przekształcają się w shogaole o silniejszym działaniu przeciwzapalnym. TCM nazywa to "jednym źródłem, wieloma właściwościami" - nauka dodaje precyzyjną farmakologię.

Regularnie stosowany imbir reorganizuje mikrobiotę jelitową, zwiększając populacje bakterii probiotycznych z rodzaju Lactobacillus i Bifidobacterium (PMID: 37690779). Jednocześnie poprawia kontrolę glikemii - metaanaliza pokazuje redukcję HbA1c o około 1% u osób z cukrzycą typu 2 (PMID: 29541142). To właśnie te "ukryte" efekty układają się w "harmonizację systemu", o której mówi TCM.

Jak stosować (protokół oparty na badaniach):
Świeży imbir: 10-20g dziennie (kawałek 4-5 cm), pokrojony w plastry. Zalej ciepłą wodą 80-90°C, parz 5-10 minut. Pij powoli.

Podziel na 2 porcje: rano na czczo wspiera metabolizm i aktywację układu trawiennego, wieczorem (2h przed snem) działa kojąco i regeneracyjnie.

Możesz dodać cytrynę lub miód, ale dopiero gdy napój ostygnie poniżej 40°C. Efekty metaboliczne i przeciwzapalne widoczne są po 8-12 tygodniach regularnego stosowania, nie po tygodniu.

⚠️ Przeciwwskazania: leki przeciwzakrzepowe, planowana operacja (przerwij 7 dni przed), ciąża wysokiego ryzyka. Zawsze konsultuj z lekarzem.

text:
‼️Lies hier unten weiter👇🏼

Schreibe „ja“ in die Kommentare, wenn du Zugang zu unserer kostenlosen Gesundheits Gruppe zum Austauschen haben möchtest.

🦷 Was die Zähne zeigen:
Zahnschmerz bei Berührung = Zahnwurzelentzündung
Kälte, süss- & sauer-empfindlich = Freiliegende Zahnhälse
Tonnenzähne = Lueshinweis
Zahnschmerz bei starkem Druck, kalt und sehr heiss = Zahnwurzelentzündung (Pulpitis)
Zahnschmerz bei Druck und Klopfen und heiss, nicht aber bei Kälte = Granulom

👄 Was der Mund uns sagen kann:
Voller roter Mund:
Beim Mann = Neigung zu Impotenz, Feminismus
Bei der Frau = Neigung zu Erkrankung der Keimdrüsen
Brauner Mundhof = Darmerkrankungen
Blasser, schmaler Mund bei Frauen = Östrogenmangel, Dysmenorrhoe
Lippencyanose = Herzinsuffizienz

👀 Was die Schläfen sagen:
Stark vorstehende, geschlängelte Schläfenarterie und rotes Gesicht = Arteriitis temporalis, essentieller Hochdruck, Nierenbelastung
Mit blassem Gesicht = Renaler Hochdruck, Arterioskle-rose, Cerebralsklerose
Mit Cyanose = Obere Hohlvenenstauung

ℹ️ Zur Information: dieses Wissen habe ich mir selbstverständlich nicht ausgedacht, sondern es entstammt der Pathophysiognomie:
Das ist das Lesen von sichtbaren Zeichen, die zeigen, wo im System gerade etwas blockiert, überfordert oder aus dem Gleichgewicht geraten ist.

Wenn du genaueres dazu erfahren möchtest empfehle ich dir das Buch „Krankheiten aus dem Gesicht erkennen“ von Kurt Tepperwein.

post_owner.name: Biohacking | Zdrowie + Nauka 🔬
text:
Chińczycy mają przysłowie: "Po posiłku przejdź 100 kroków, a dożyjesz 99 lat". Brzmi jak ludowa mądrość? Współczesna nauka mówi: to działa.

W medycynie chińskiej śledziona jest organem odpowiedzialnym za "transformację i transport" pokarmu. Po jedzeniu energia Qi koncentruje się w układzie trawiennym. Jeśli pozostajesz w bezruchu, energia stagnuje. Pojawia się wilgoć (湿, shī) - wzdęcia, ciężkość, ospałość. Delikatny ruch rozprowadza Qi po ciele, przywracając równowagę między Yin i Yang.

Brzmi ezoteryczne? Fizjologia mówi to samo, tylko innymi słowami. Badania z George Washington University pokazują, że 15-minutowy spacer po posiłku obniża glukozę o około 10%. Skurcze mięśni aktywują transportery GLUT4, które pobierają cukier niezależnie od insuliny. Kluczowe dla insulinooporności.

Umiarkowany spacer zwiększa perfuzję jelit, stymuluje nerw błędny i przyspiesza perystaltykę. Meta-analiza z 2024 roku (Journal of Sport and Health Science) pokazuje, że aktywność fizyczna zmniejsza ryzyko choroby refluksowej przełyku (GERD) o około 20%, a 150 minut aktywności tygodniowo może zmniejszyć to ryzyko nawet o 72% (PMID: 38552714)

Jak to wygląda w praktyce? W Chinach o 19:00 wszystkie parki ożywają. Rodziny, starsi ludzie spacerują po kolacji. Na placach tańczą starsze panie. Żywa tradycja łącząca zdrowie z więzią społeczną.

Jakie optimum? Rozpocznij 10-15 minut po posiłku, idź spokojnie 2-4 km/h przez 15-30 minut. Systematyczne przeglądy badań pokazują, że każde dodatkowe 1000 kroków dziennie wiąże się z 5-21% redukcją ryzyka chorób sercowo-naczyniowych (PMID: 32563261)

Tradycyjne "100 kroków" to zaledwie 75 metrów, symboliczne minimum. Współczesna interpretacja? 1000-2000 kroków daje pełny efekt.

Co fascynujące: medycyna chińska opisywała te mechanizmy setki lat temu językiem energii, my dziś potwierdzamy to glukometrami i badaniami perfuzji. Różne języki, ta sama prawda.

A Ty? Spacer po kolacji czy kanapa? 🚶

✨️GLOW TEA RECIPE✨️ 

This tea is not only going to help you glow from the inside out but it's also amazing to pair with your collagen rich foods for plumpy skin.  It helps with numerous health concerns and will nourish and give your body immunity boosting properties. 

*This recipe is for a big batch so please adjust to your needs and taste (half or quarter it)* 

INGREDIENTS:
24 large jujube pitted
165 grams ginger (started at 196grams, cut down to 165 after slicing off some skin)
160 Oz filtered water (20 cups)
8 grams chrysanthemum 
15 grams rose buds
15 grams goji berries 

1. In a large pot of water add the jujubes and ginger. Turn the heat to high.
2. Once it starts boiling, turn the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes with cover on.
3. Add dried chrysanthemum and rose buds and simmer for an additional 10 minutes with cover on.
4. Turn off the heat and add in goji berries. Allow the goji berries to soak in the hot liquid for 5 minutes. 
5. Strain out the debri and enjoy right away. 
6. You can also leave it to cool completely before straining it to allow it to become more potent. 
7. Place into the fridge for up to 1.5 weeks.

post_owner.name: Biohacking | Zdrowie + Nauka 🔬
text:
Pijesz wodę źle i nawet o tym nie wiesz. Te 5 błędów powoli niszczą twoje trawienie, metabolizm i energię życiową.

Tradycyjna Medycyna Chińska od tysięcy lat przestrzega przed błędami w piciu wody, które osłabiają "ogień trawienny". Współczesna nauka wreszcie wyjaśnia mechanizmy, które stoją za tą starożytną mądrością.

BŁĄD 1: Zimna woda
TCM mówi o niszczeniu Yang Qi żołądka. Nauka potwierdza, że zimna woda powoduje wazokonstrykcję w ścianie żołądka, opóźnia opróżnianie i obniża aktywność enzymów trawiennych. Pij ciepłą wodę 35-40°C (nie wymaga energii na ogrzanie, wspiera metabolizm).

BŁĄD 2: Picie zbyt szybko
Badania pokazują, że powolne picie (200ml co 15-20 min) zwiększa absorbcje wody. Nerki filtrują max 800-1000ml/godz, a nadmiar trafia do moczu bez hydratacji komórek. Popijaj małymi łykami.

BŁĄD 3: Picie podczas jedzenia
TCM: woda rozcieńcza soki żołądkowe. Nauka: małe ilości (100-150ml) są OK, ale duże objętości (300ml+) przyspieszają opróżnianie żołądka, skracają trawienie, powodują wzdęcia. Szczególnie problemowe przy GERD i dyspepsji.

BŁĄD 4: Brak wody przed snem
150-200ml ciepłej wody 30-60 min przed snem wspomaga nocną detoksyfikację nerek, zapobiega zagęszczeniu krwi.

BŁĄD 5: Niewłaściwa ilość
Za mało = odwodnienie, kamienie nerkowe, zaparcia. Za dużo = hiponatremia, obciążenie nerek. Norma: kobiety ~2L, mężczyźni ~2,5-3L z napojów. Wskaźnik: jasny, słomkowy kolor moczu.

Praktyczny protokół:
🌅 Rano: 300-400ml ciepłej wody na czczo
💧 Przed posiłkami: 150-200ml (20-30 min wcześniej)
🍽️ Podczas jedzenia: max 100-150ml
⏰ Co 30-45 min: małe porcje 100-200ml
🌙 Przed snem: 150-200ml ciepłej wody

Wdrażaj stopniowo przez 21 dni. Obserwuj kolor moczu, energię, trawienie.

Zapisz ten post i zacznij dziś. Twoje ciało poczuje różnicę w tydzień.

From 7–11 PM, your spleen and liver are supposed to switch into repair mode: restoring skin, rebalancing hormones, improving circulation, and rebuilding the energy you burned during the day.

That’s why you wake up puffy, tired, inflamed, and less resilient over time.

If you want real anti-aging from a TCM perspective, protect your evening routine. Eat earlier, disconnect earlier, and let your body follow the organ clock the way it was designed.

Does black sesame prevent gray hair? In traditional Chinese medicine, black sesame is known as a longevity food that nourishes your kidneys and maintains dark hair.

But there’s actually no definitive evidence that black sesame keeps your hair dark! Our hair color is due to the pigment melanin, which is produced by melanocytes. 

As we age, our melanocytes produce less melanin and there is nothing yet on the market for reversing gray hair. Potential solutions would involve melanocyte stem cell regeneration and proper localization of these cells in our hair follicle niche to revive hair color!

What we do know is black sesame is still a great source of calcium, fiber, and other antioxidants that have been shown to be anti-inflammatory!

Cold weather weakens our core fire — the source of warmth, libido, fertility, and energy.
To replenish essence, use: black sesame, black beans, cordyceps, walnuts, black wood ear fungus, seaweed, Chinese yam, burdock root, sweet potatoes, carrots, turnips, rye

Even though winter is a yin season, heaters and cold winds can dry us out.

Cold causes qi and blood to tighten and stagnate leading to cold extremities, cramps, and aches.
Warm and move the system with: goji berries, ginger, dried red dates, chicken broths, dang gui, cinnamon, peppercorn, chives, scallions

🛑RELATÓRIO DO TCM APONTA FALHAS GRAVES NA SAÚDE

Um relatório do TCM (Tribunal de Contas dos Municípios) revelou uma série de irregularidades preocupantes na gestão da saúde, que colocam em risco a qualidade do atendimento e a transparência do uso do dinheiro público.

📌 Entre os problemas encontrados pelos auditores estão:
	•	Presença de mofo e infiltrações em unidades de saúde;
	•	Fiação exposta e falta de acessibilidade;
	•	Equipes médicas irregulares, com número reduzido de profissionais;
	•	Inexistência de ar-condicionado adequado para manter vacinas e insumos refrigerados.

Além disso, o TCM apontou que a prefeitura não realizou concurso público há mais de 10 anos, mantendo grande parte dos profissionais em caráter temporário, o que contraria a Constituição Federal. De 855 trabalhadores analisados, apenas 286 tinham vínculo efetivo, e mesmo assim foram identificadas falhas de capacitação.

📌 Outro ponto crítico citado no relatório:
A gestão deixou de enviar os relatórios quadrimestrais de saúde ao Conselho Municipal de Saúde e à Câmara de Vereadores, documento obrigatório por lei federal.
➡️ Essa falha compromete o controle social e a transparência dos gastos públicos.

Também foram registrados:
	•	Dados desatualizados no Cadastro Nacional de Estabelecimentos de Saúde (CNES);
	•	Falta de protocolos de encaminhamento para serviços especializados, prejudicando os pacientes que precisam de atendimento mais complexo.

🔍 O relatório coloca em evidência a necessidade urgente de melhorias estruturais, administrativas e de transparência para garantir um serviço digno à população.

text:
🚨🚨 Em corredores que deveriam respirar cuidado, equipamentos desgastados ameaçam fazer o contrário, es m vez de curar, podem aprofundar o adoecimento de quem depende do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) em Lauro de Freitas, na Região Metropolitana de Salvador (RMS).

A Bnews Premium teve acesso ao relatório da 3ª Diretoria de Controle Externo (DCE) do Tribunal de Contas dos Municípios da Bahia (TCM-BA), que detalha problemas encontrados em cinco Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBS) e Unidades de Saúde Familiar (UFS) de Lauro de Freitas.  

A auditoria do tribunal apontou estruturas precarizadas, falta de médicos e ausência de equipamentos essenciais para a conservação de vacinas e outros. Esse levantamento integra uma Auditoria Temática realizada em 2023, relatada pelo conselheiro Nelson Pelegrino, julgada em novembro de 2025.  

Entre as falhas apontadas estão a presença de mofo, infiltrações, fiação exposta, falta de acessibilidade, ausência de equipes fixas, número reduzido de profissionais e inexistência de ar-condicionado adequado para manter vacinas e insumos refrigerados.

Um dos pontos mais críticos identificados pelo TCM foi a falta de concurso público por mais de dez anos. O tribunal constatou que a maioria dos médicos e demais profissionais das UBS atuavam em caráter temporário, em desacordo com a Constituição Federal. Dos 855 trabalhadores analisados, apenas 286 tinham vínculo efetivo e, mesmo entre eles, os auditores encontraram falhas de capacitação.

Segundo o TCM, a gestão de Moema também descumpriu normas federais, incluindo a obrigatoriedade de enviar os relatórios quadrimestrais de saúde ao Conselho Municipal de Saúde e à Câmara de Vereadores. Essas falhas, segundo o Tribunal, comprometem o controle social da gestão e a transparência dos gastos públicos.

Outro problema apresentando no relatório foram os dados desatualizados no Cadastro Nacional de Estabelecimentos de Saúde (CNES) e a ausência de protocolos de encaminhamento de pacientes para serviços especializados.

Chinese exercises like Qigong, Tai Chi, Ba Duan Jin, and Five Animal Frolics are ancient healing movements rooted in Traditional Chinese Medicine. 
They focus on breath, slow flow, mindfulness, and energy circulation (Qi).

✨ What They Do to Your Body

1️⃣ Improve Qi circulation
These slow, rhythmic movements help release stuck energy, calm your nervous system, and improve overall vitality.

2️⃣ Balance the autonomic nervous system
They shift the body from “fight or flight” to rest & digest, reducing stress hormones like cortisol. Lower cortisol = better metabolism.

3️⃣ Enhance joint mobility
Gentle, fluid motions lubricate the joints, improve flexibility, and reduce stiffness perfect if you sit a lot.

4️⃣ Strengthen muscles without strain
They build deep postural muscles, improve spinal alignment, and increase stability.

5️⃣ Improve lung capacity
Qigong breathwork increases oxygenation and strengthens the diaphragm. Better oxygen = better cellular function.

6️⃣ Boost digestion
Many movements are designed to massage the internal organs and stimulate digestive fire.

⏳ How Many Times to Practice?

👌 Beginners:
10–15 minutes daily
(You’ll see changes in stress levels within a week)

🌿 For weight loss & energy balance:
20–30 minutes daily or 4–5x a week

💛 For deep healing (stress, digestion, hormones):
30–40 minutes daily
Qigong masters say even 10 minutes daily is more effective than 1 hour once a week.

text:
Ciepła woda o poranku - czy to tylko moda wellness, czy coś więcej?

Tradycyjna Medycyna Chińska i Ajurweda od tysięcy lat zalecają picie ciepłej wody na czczo. Współczesna fizjologia zaczyna wreszcie wyjaśniać mechanizmy, które wcześniej były jedynie intuicją.

Kiedy temperatura wody zbliża się do ciepłoty ciała (36-40°C), nie obciążasz organizmu energią potrzebną do jej „podgrzania". Badania Sun et al. (1988) potwierdzają, że ciepłe płyny przyspieszają perystaltykę jelit i skracają czas opróżniania żołądka. W praktyce? Łatwiejsza ewakuacja, lepsza detoksyfikacja przez naturalną aktywność jelit.

TCM nazywa to „rozpalaniem ognia trawiennego" i nie jest to tylko metafora. Ciepło pobudza receptor TRPV1 w ścianie żołądka, co zwiększa przepływ krwi do błony śluzowej i aktywuje trawienie już przed pierwszym kęsem. Ajurweda dodaje, że ciepła woda balansuje Vata (element powietrza), która rano jest naturalnie wzmożona i może powodować uczucie niespokoju czy wzdęcia.

Skąd w ogóle wzięło się przekonanie o „wypłukiwaniu toksyn"? Z ajurwedyjskiej koncepcji ama - produktów niedotrawienia, które gromadzą się w ciele i blokują przepływ energii. Współczesna nauka tłumaczy to inaczej: odpowiednie nawodnienie wspiera nerki w filtrowaniu krwi (wartość GFR wzrasta przy optymalnej wolemii), ułatwia limfie transport produktów przemiany materii, a wątrobie - reakcje detoksykacji fazy II. Gorąca woda nie "rozpuszcza toksyn", ale optymalizuje naturalne szlaki ich eliminacji przez układ wydalniczy.

W medycynie integracyjnej patrzymy na to holistycznie: prosty rytuał poranny obniża kortyzol, daje moment mindfulness i sygnalizuje organizmowi „czas się obudzić". Nie zastąpi diety ani ruchu, ale tworzy fundament pod zdrowe nawyki.

Jaka temperatura? 36-45°C, taka, żeby nie parzła. Ile? Szklanka wystarczy. Kiedy? Przed kawą, przed jedzeniem. I uwaga, jeśli pijesz bardzo gorące napoje (>60°C), zwiększasz ryzyko uszkodzenia przełyku (Islami et al., 2009).

Czy ty pijesz ciepłą wodę rano? 💧

Have you ever used dream analysis to build a pattern diagnosis?

Underneath most of the woo-woo stuff is actually a strong truth, once we know how to find it...

In dreams the subconscious is speaking. Sometimes it's random nonsense, but when patterns emerge we do well to take note. For example:

Recurring dreams about being chased, hunted, eaten, zombies etc can indicate hidden pathogens in the body. The immune system is struggling and asking for help.

Recurring dreams about food, as well as resources, a home, support etc can indicate digestive issues. Look for dampness, food stagnation, spleen qi deficiency...

Recurring dreams of being trapped, climbing trees, biting things/people etc can indicate liver qi constraint...

Recurring dreams about blood, children, family, being stabbed etc can indicate blood stasis. Especially for female reproductive complaints...

Should we base an entire pattern diagnosis on a dream? Not really. But can we look into what the subconscious is asking for as another data point? Yes.

Can we share some of this with the patient so they feel more connected to their own subconscious and their own body? Yes.

Winter zet alles op pauze, behalve je gedachten. Buiten is het donker, je lijf is moe… maar vanbinnen blijft alles doordraaien.

In de Chinese geneeskunde is de winter het seizoen van de Nierfunctiekring.
Dat systeem gaat over angst, diepliggende stress, wilskracht en gronding.

Als de Nierqi uit balans raakt, voel je dat niet alleen in je onderrug of als koude voeten, maar ook als dat onrustige gevoel dat je maar niet “uit” krijgt.

Op die momenten gebruik ik graag Nier 4. Dit punt ligt net achter en onder je binnenenkel, aan de binnenkant van je voet.

In TCM wordt Nier 4 verbonden met:

➡️het kalmeren van angst en innerlijke onrust,

➡️het ondersteunen van de Nierenergie in de winter,

➡️en het gevoel dat je weer terugzakt in je lichaam in plaats van te blijven hangen in je hoofd.

Hoe je het kunt gebruiken:

Zoek het punt op achter je binnenenkel.

Druk zacht met je duim of wijsvinger en maak kleine cirkels.

Blijf een minuut rustig ademen naar je buik en voel wat er verandert.

Zie het niet als een magische knop,
maar als een klein dagelijks ritueel om jezelf in donkere, koude dagen
weer wat veiligheid, warmte en gronding te geven.

Deze reel beschrijft de TCM-visie en vervangt geen medisch onderzoek.
Bij aanhoudende of ernstige klachten: altijd je huisarts raadplegen.

60 minutes? 90 minutes? 5 minutes? 

The practice models we pick up in school are great to get started, but eventually we need to outgrow them.

Some intakes are highly involved. Complex chronic issues with autoimmunity, a pile of diagnoses and symptoms, a 2 inch stack of lab reports in a manilla folder, a lot to cover...

A little kid with an ear infection. A retired lady who tweaked her back playing pickleball. A baseball pitcher with shoulder pain.

Segundo matéria publicada pelo Portal A Tarde, o Tribunal de Contas dos Municípios da Bahia determinou a suspensão imediata do contrato de locação de veículos utilizado pela Prefeitura de Jaguarari. A decisão bloqueia novos pagamentos e também impede qualquer tentativa de prorrogação da dispensa emergencial que vinha sendo usada para manter o serviço ativo.

A medida foi tomada após uma denúncia formal apresentada pela COOPTRASB, que apontou possíveis irregularidades na contratação da frota. Diante das informações levantadas, o TCM-BA identificou risco concreto para o erário municipal e, por isso, adotou a cautelar para evitar que a situação avance sem esclarecimentos.

A decisão também destaca que a prefeitura vinha utilizando dispensa emergencial para manter o contrato, mecanismo que, segundo o tribunal, não pode ser prorrogado nessas condições. A suspensão vale imediatamente e permanece até que o mérito seja analisado.

O prefeito Antônio Ferreira do Nascimento foi notificado e terá 20 dias para apresentar defesa formal. Após esse prazo, o TCM deve decidir se mantém a suspensão, se revoga a medida ou se aprofunda a investigação com novas análises.

O Portal A Tarde também informou que a Prefeitura de Jaguarari foi procurada para comentar o caso, mas ainda não enviou resposta. O processo segue tramitando no Tribunal de Contas, que acompanha cada etapa da contratação e aguarda os esclarecimentos da gestão municipal.

post_owner.name: RIIKKA SIUSLUOTO
text:
Mitä akupunktiovastaanotollani tapahtuu — oikeasti? 

Akupunktio on yhdistelmä tarkkaa havainnointia ja kehon luonnollisen palautumiskyvyn käynnistämistä. Mitään mystistä siinä ei ole. 

1. Keskustelu
Kysyn oireista, mutta myös mm. unesta, stressistä, jaksamisesta. Ne kertovat, miten hermosto ja energia kulkevat.

2. Kieli ja pulssi
Käytän kahta työkalua, diagnosoin kielen ja pulssin
– Kieli kertoo mm. ruoansulatuksen ja kehon lämpötilan säätelyn.
– Pulssi kertoo, missä kohtaa kuormitus näkyy, ja missä energia pysähtyy.

3. Hoito, joka lähtee sinusta
Valitsen pisteet niiden perusteella, mitä keho viestii – ei valmiin kaavan mukaan.

Tavoite on yksinkertainen:
vapauttaa virtausta, rauhoittaa hermostoa ja keventää oloa.

4. Neulat. Monet kysyy, sattuuko neulat? Neulat ei satu, ne ovat todella ohuita ja monia et edes huomaa, kun ne laitetaan. 

Kun neulat ovat paikoillaan, keho siirtyy luonnollisesti lepo-tilaan. Usein ensimmäinen merkki siitä on se, että hartiat laskevat ilman että huomaat. Monet nukahtavat tai ovat syvässä rentoutuneessa tilassa ja ajantaju usein pysähtyy. 

5. Jatkohoito 
Annan mukaan vain sen, mikä aidosti tukee sinua:
ehkä yksi hengitysharjoitus tai yksi akupainantapiste — ei mitään laajaa tehtävälistaa.
Mahdollisia ruoka-ohjeita. 

Akupunktio on kehon kuuntelemista datan, tuntemusten ja kokemuksen kautta.

text:
Vi lever i en modern tid där vi ständigt söker nya lösningar… samtidigt som vi ignorerar det som alltid funnits.

Vi har byggt hela vår förståelse av kroppen baserat på de senaste 100 åren.
Modeller som delar upp, kategoriserar och isolerar. Muskler för sig. Organ för sig. Känslor för sig.

Men kroppen fungerar inte så.
Och har aldrig gjort det.

För 2 000–3 000 år sedan beskrev man ett system där energi, känslor, fascia, muskler, organ och rörelse flödade som ett och samma nät.
Ett system där stagnation inte var ett “problem”, utan ett stopp i flödet.
Ett system där helheten hade mer intelligens än delarna någonsin kan visa.

Och ju mer forskning vi har idag på fascia, bioelektricitet, piezoelektriska effekter, strukturerat vatten och meridianernas anatomi…
…desto tydligare blir det att det uråldriga aldrig var mystiskt,
vi hade bara inte tekniken att förstå det.

Your nails and fingertips are tiny diagnostic windows — subtle, but incredibly honest. They reveal what your blood, your organs, and even your metabolism are doing long before symptoms become loud. 

💅🏻 Clubbed fingertips, for example, are a classic sign of chronic low oxygenation and often appear in smokers or those with long-term lung or heart issues. 

💅🏻 Uneven nail color tells a similar story: tissues not getting enough oxygen. 

💅🏻 White spots or white lines are frequently linked to low zinc. 

💅🏻 Missing lunulae — those little half-moons — point toward possible iron or vitamin B deficiencies. 

💅🏻 Darkened skin folds around the fingers can indicate trouble with insulin metabolism, while inflamed cuticles and frequent hangnails usually reflect low-grade inflammation and poor protein intake. 

💅🏻 And yellowish nails? In most cases, tobacco exposure. 

The body leaves clues everywhere; the nails just happen to be some of the most straightforward ones to read. When you know how to interpret these patterns, early prevention becomes simple — and your overall vitality becomes much easier to protect

mensen die denken dat hun overdenken of rampscenario’s “gewoon hun persoonlijkheid” is.

Milt versterken, Lever ontspannen, Qi laten zakken, Shen tot rust brengen.
Dat is de basis.

text:
Cuando llega el frío, nuestro cuerpo necesita un poquito de calor interno para mantenerse fuerte.
Por eso preparo estos caramelos caseros de jengibre y miel: prácticos, naturales y perfectos para apoyar la inmunidad en otoño e invierno.

En Medicina Tradicional China, el jengibre calienta el Yang, mueve el Qi y expulsa el frío; la miel nutre, suaviza y protege la garganta.
Un gesto sencillo para sentirte más contenida y protegida durante el día. ✨🍯

Ingredientes
	•	100 g de jengibre fresco
	•	200 g de miel
	•	(Opcional) Unas gotas de limón

Preparación
	1.	Pela y ralla el jengibre.
	2.	Colócalo en un cazo con un poquito de agua y llévalo al fuego para extraer su principio activo.
	•	Déjalo calentar unos minutos hasta que suelte la esencia y el aroma sea intenso.
	3.	Cuela la mezcla: retira la pulpa del jengibre y reserva solo el agua concentrada del jengibre.
	4.	Añade la miel a ese líquido y cocina a fuego muy lento durante 20–25 minutos, removiendo con suavidad.
	5.	Sabrás que está listo cuando la mezcla espese y tenga textura de sirope denso.
	6.	Retira del fuego, deja reposar unos minutos y luego forma los caramelos sobre papel de hornear o moldes de silicona.
	7.	Deja enfriar hasta que se solidifiquen y guárdalos en un frasco hermético.

Una combinación cálida y suave para acompañarte todo el otoño e invierno. 🍃🔥

9 Things I Wish I Knew About Mental Health in Perimenopause and Menopause, According to Traditional Chinese Medicine

1️⃣ Hormonal Shifts Affect More Than Just Your Period
In TCM, declining Kidney Yin and Blood during menopause can lead to symptoms like anxiety, irritability, and insomnia—long before your period fully stops.

2️⃣ Your Liver Influences Your Mood
The Liver is responsible for the smooth flow of Qi and emotions. If Liver Qi stagnates (often from stress), it can trigger mood swings, anger, or depression.

3️⃣ Sleep Is Your First Medicine
Poor sleep depletes Heart Blood and disturbs the Shen (mind/spirit). Perimenopause often brings disrupted sleep, which amplifies emotional symptoms.

4️⃣ You’re Not Just ‘More Emotional’, Your Heart May Be Out of Balance
In TCM, the Heart houses the Shen. If the Heart is affected by Heat, Blood deficiency, or stagnation, it can manifest as anxiety, racing thoughts, or feeling unsettled.

5️⃣ Digestive Health Impacts Mental Health
A weakened Spleen leads to Dampness, which can cloud the mind and contribute to brain fog, fatigue, and low motivation.

6️⃣ Yin Nourishment Calms the Mind
Yin deficiency, common in menopause, can lead to restlessness, agitation, and night sweats that disturb sleep and mental clarity.

7️⃣ External Stress Hits Harder Now
Your resilience may feel lower. TCM sees this as a depletion of foundational energy (Kidney Jing), making recovery from stress slower and more emotionally draining.

8️⃣ You Might Feel Lonely or Untethered; and That’s a Spirit Imbalance
In Chinese medicine, feeling disconnected, isolated, or ungrounded can reflect a Heart or Kidney imbalance. It’s not just in your head, it’s in your Qi.

9️⃣ You’re Not Meant to Push Through This Alone
In TCM, menopause is a profound life shift, not a problem to fix, but a transition to be supported. Community, nourishment, rest, and gentle practices are key to protecting your mental health.

Save this for when you need a reminder that what you’re feeling is real, and there’s another way to navigate it.

Traditional Indian medicine Ayurveda and TCM have a lot in common, the main difference being that TCM has been researched more, essentially since 1955 when the Academy of TCM was founded, while scientific studies of Ayurveda have only been conducted in recent decades.

In Sweden and much of the Western world, the perception is that acupuncture can only help with pain. However, thousands of RCT studies (randomised controlled trials, considered in Western medicine to have the highest evidential value when evaluating a treatment) have shown that acupuncture is effective against a huge number of conditions. 

We learned this yesterday at an institute for TCM in Beijing, where the pictures were also taken.

Love Maclee Gu Qi Kitchen — Metal ➝ Water Seasonal Tonic 

Every year when Metal exhales its last breath and Water begins to rise, I make this simple tonic of American ginseng, red dates, and goji berries soaked in Er Guo Tou.
It’s my way of helping the body descend, soften, and store — exactly what this season asks of us.

In TCM, late autumn is a time when the Lungs release and the Kidneys gather.
This tonic supports that shift:

• American Ginseng cool-nourishes Lung & Kidney Yin so we don’t dry out or burn out as the weather sharpens. It hydrates from within, supporting the Lungs — the organ that governs the skin’s moisture, texture, and glow.

And then there is Er Guo Tou (二锅头) —
a traditional Chinese grain spirit whose name means “Second Pot Head,” referring to the pure, clean middle cut of the distillation.
Warm and penetrating, it acts as a natural solvent and messenger, helping the herbs travel deeper into the channels while gently warming what winter tries to chill.

I use this tonic by adding one small spoonful to broths, teas, or cooking for a subtle lift of Qi and quiet nourishment.
Not a drink to get tipsy — a seasonal medicine to keep the inner fire alive and the skin protected through the colder, drier months.

As we enter the darker, colder months, our medicines shift deeper — warming, storing, and protecting our Yin.

Stillness before strength.

The lymphatic system is one of the most underrated heroes of women’s health. It’s your body’s purification network—clearing waste, moving immune cells, regulating inflammation, and keeping your tissues hydrated and nourished

But unlike the cardiovascular system, it has no pump. It depends entirely on you: your breath, your movement, your hydration, your daily habits

Deep breathing creates a natural vacuum that pulls lymph upward through the diaphragm. Hydration keeps lymph fluid thin enough to move. Physical activity squeezes lymph along its vessels, like gentle pumps built into your muscles. And rebounding adds a playful, low-impact boost to circulation that your lymph absolutely loves

When your lymph flows, everything feels lighter—your energy, your mood, your skin, your digestion. When it stagnates, you feel it: puffiness, heaviness, brain fog, fatigue, swelling, inflammation

Supporting your lymph isn’t complicated. It just requires presence. Breathe deeper. Move daily. Hydrate consistently. Add practices like dry brushing, contrast showers, sauna, and massage when you can. Small rituals, big impact

The Science Behind Masaru Emoto’s Water Experiments

What if the words you speak could shape the world inside your body?
Masaru Emoto’s work on water molecules sparked one of the most important conversations in mind–body science. His research suggested that water exposed to positive words, music, or intentions formed harmonious crystalline structures, while water exposed to negative language showed chaotic, disorganized patterns.

Even though his methodology has been debated, his findings opened a meaningful doorway into how our emotional states may influence our physiology. Considering that the human body is mostly water, this perspective becomes even more significant.

Modern fields like cymatics, vibrational biology, and neurophysiology now explore similar ideas. We know sound frequencies alter matter, emotions shift biochemistry, and intention affects the nervous system. Emoto’s work mirrors what many healing traditions have known for centuries, and what current science continues to explore: energy matters.

Here is the practical part.
Let your water become a mirror of your state. Speak to it before drinking it. Play music near it. Hold the bottle and take one mindful breath. Observe how your mood shifts when you add intention to something as simple as hydration.

If you want to take it further, play with two glasses. Label one with a positive word and the other with a stressful word. Notice how you respond to each one. Your body often feels the difference first, even if the molecules are invisible to the eye.

text:
Asthma is a long term respiratory condition that manifests through repeated episodes of wheezing, coughing, chest tightness, and difficulty breathing. The frequency and severity of these symptoms can vary among individuals and are often triggered by infections, stress or environmental factors. From a modern medical perspective, asthma results from chronic inflammation and hypersensitivity of the airways. However, in some patients, symptoms persist even without an active infection or strong external trigger. They may experience shortness of breath after mild exertion, low voice, spontaneous sweating, and a tendency to catch colds easily. This pattern is recognized in Traditional Chinese Medicine as Lung deficiency syndrome, where the Lung’s vital energy (Qi) is weakened and unable to perform its function of dispersing and descending properly.

From the TCM viewpoint, Lung deficiency asthma is rooted in an insufficiency of Lung Qi that may arise from prolonged illness, overexertion, chronic cough or constitutional weakness. The Lungs govern Qi and respiration. When Lung Qi is weak, the airways lose their ability to stay open and clear, leading to recurrent shortness of breath and shallow breathing. Typical symptoms include persistent mild wheezing that worsens with fatigue, low or weak voice, spontaneous sweating, aversion to wind, and a pale complexion. Treatment focuses on tonifying Lung Qi and strengthening the body’s resistance. 

Commonly prescribed formulas include Bu Fei Tang and Shen Ge San, tailored according to individual conditions. Acupuncture points such as Fei Shu (BL13) and Tai Yuan (LU9) are used to tonify Lung Qi and regulate breathing. Moxibustion may be applied to provide warmth and strengthen the Lung’s energy. From a lifestyle perspective, patients should avoid overexertion, ensure adequate rest, and protect themselves from sudden weather changes. A balanced diet that includes warm and easily digestible foods such as soups, congee, and lean meats helps nourish Lung Qi. Gentle breathing exercises, Tai Chi, and Qi Gong are also beneficial to strengthen lung capacity and promote relaxation.

✨ TCM Hair-Healing Trio: Black Sesame, Black Rice & Black Soybeans ✨
If you’ve been dealing with hair thinning, shedding, white hair or to prevent it all, this TCM trio is your new best friend. In Traditional Chinese Medicine, hair health is connected to the kidneys, the blood, and overall “life energy” — so instead of treating hair problems from the outside, TCM goes straight to the root (literally).
Why they work:
* Black Sesame: Nourishes the liver & kidneys, helps slow down graying, and promotes shiny, strong hair.
* Black Rice: Full of antioxidants to protect hair follicles and boost scalp health.
* Black Soybeans: Rich in protein, vitamins, and minerals to support hair growth and improve circulation to the scalp.

All you have to do is gather:
- 1cup sesame seeds
- 1/2cup black soybeans
- 1/2cup black rice
- Food processor (better if you have a Vitamix)
- Airtight container
- Pan or wok

1. Rinse all the ingredients (separately) and let air dry on a towel
2. Toast each ingredient in a pan (separately) WITHOUT OIL, stirring frequently, making sure not to burn:
3. Black soybeans toast for 20-30 minutes on med-low heat (when the beans are popped and browning and there’s a nutty aroma)
4. black rice toast for 20 mins on medium and then low heat (until the colour changes without burning and nutty aroma) 
5. black sesame 3-6 mins on low heat (until the seed can be easily crushed between fingers and nutty aroma)
6. Let each ingredient cool down, then turn into powder using a food processor or Vitamix, mix into an airtight container
7. Enjoy daily, one spoonful as it is or add it to yogurt, milk, hot water and sugar, smoothies, soups, etc.

Goiânia investe R$ 828 milhões na saúde em 2025

A Prefeitura de Goiânia, sob a gestão de Sandro Mabel, ultrapassou R$ 828 milhões em investimentos na saúde apenas neste ano, segundo dados oficiais.

→ Esse valor representa 20,76% do orçamento municipal, muito acima do mínimo constitucional exigido (15 %).
→ Foram quitadas dívidas de R$ 276 milhões, reaberto o Centro de Referência em Ortopedia (CROF) e ampliadas equipes do SAMU com 22 novas ambulâncias.
→ Nas maternidades municipais, o novo modelo de gestão permitiu retomar atendimentos de urgência, cirurgias eletivas e exames.
→ A atenção primária (consultas ambulatoriais) já ultrapassa 871 mil atendimentos, e as emergências somam quase 981 mil no ano. 

----------------------------------------

Fechamento de CMEI Orlando Alves Carneiro é suspenso pelo TCM-GO

O Tribunal de Contas dos Municípios de Goiás (TCM-GO) referendou uma medida cautelar que suspende o fechamento do CMEI Orlando Alves Carneiro, localizado no Setor Campinas, em Goiânia. 

→ A decisão ocorreu após denúncia da vereadora Aava Santiago, que questionou a antecipação do encerramento das atividades da escola infantil.
→ Na medida, o TCM exige que a prefeitura apresente um plano detalhado para remanejamento de alunos e servidores e justificativas técnicas para o fechamento. 
→ O prédio precisa comprovar condições seguras de operação, como alvarás e rotas de fuga, antes que qualquer decisão definitiva seja tomada.
→ A cautelar se mantém até que a prefeitura apresente estudos e propostas concretas, sob risco de nova decisão do tribunal.

A educação infantil está em debate: a suspensão do fechamento garante tempo para planejamento e participação da comunidade.

post_owner.name: Miko Wang
text:
Galbitang (Korean beef short rib soup) so good! Baby girl loved the beef too 🤎

Ingredients
• 1 pack beef short ribs (6–7 large pieces) — I got mine from Costco
• 2 medium onions (halved)
• 5 green onions
• 4–6 cloves garlic
• 3–4 slices ginger
• 1 handful whole peppercorns
• 1 small Korean radish (mu), peeled & cut into chunks
• 1 egg (optional – for egg strip garnish)
• Water (enough to fully cover ribs)
• 2–3 tbsp Korean soup soy sauce (see video for the one I’m using)
• Salt & pepper (to taste)

Steps:
1. Soak the ribs in cold water for 1 hour (or overnight) to remove blood. Drain and rinse.
2. Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 2–5 minutes. Drain and rinse off any impurities.
3. Prep aromatics: halve onions, slice ginger, cut garlic. Separate green onions (white parts for broth, green parts for garnish).
4. Build the broth: Add ribs, onions, green onion whites, peppercorns, garlic, and ginger into a clean pot. Cover fully with water.
5. Bring to a boil, then reduce to low and simmer for 1 hour. Skim foam/oil.
6. Add radish now and continue to boil for 1 hour on low.
7. Remove radish, slice into bite-size pieces, add a little bit of water, and continue to boil for another 1.5–2 hours (total boiling time ~4 hours).
8. Remove aromatics (onions, peppercorns, ginger, garlic).
9. Optional: I removed some beef first to give to my 11-month-old unseasoned before I seasoned the broth.
10. Season with soup soy sauce and salt. Simmer 10 minutes.
11. Boil sweet potato noodles and rinse in cold water. I like to season the noodles with a little bit of soy sauce and salt.
12. Assemble your sliced radish, noodles, soup, and beef. Add egg strip on top with sliced green onions. Adjust salt & pepper to taste.

Enjoy!!!!

• Ułóż opuszek palca w zagłębieniu nad środkiem obojczyka.
• Zastosuj lekki, stabilny ucisk bez zagłębiania się w tkanki.
• Utrzymaj ucisk około 10–15 sekund przy spokojnym oddechu.

• Zakończ, rozluźniając barki i pozwalając Qi swobodnie opaść.

Pregnancy in Traditional Chinese Medicine is viewed as ten precious months, each guided by a specific organ system that supports both mother and baby

When a woman understands these phases, she can nourish her body with intention and create the ideal environment for new life.

🤰🏼 Month 1 begins with the Liver, where rest, emotional calm, leafy greens, and gentle sour foods support a smooth start.
🤰🏻Month 2 belongs to the Gallbladder & Dai Mai, calling for steadiness, less spice, and no overexertion.
🤰🏽Month 3 is the Heart month, encouraging joy, beauty, and peaceful thoughts to nourish the Shen.
🤰🏾Month 4 focuses on the San Jiao & blood vessels, where light, clean foods like rice help the mother’s Qi shape the foetus’ vessels.
🤰🏻Month 5 strengthens the Spleen, making warmth, balanced meals, and gentle pacing essential.
🤰🏿Month 6 activates the Stomach, supporting muscle and sinew development—strength and vitality become the theme.
🤰🏽Month 7 centres on the Lungs & Bones, with white foods, breath, and gentle movement strengthening both mother and baby.
🤰🏻Month 8 flows through the Large Intestine channel, making fibre and digestive ease crucial as the foetus’ nine orifices fully form.
🤰🏼Month 9 deepens into the Kidney system, supporting Essence as the baby’s organs complete development.
🤰🏾And Month 10 belongs to the Shen, the spirit. This is a month of calm, meditation, emotional grounding, and connection as the body prepares for birth.

In TCM, pregnancy is an energetic masterpiece. Supporting each month wisely helps create a strong, peaceful foundation for both mother and child

post_owner.name: Coach.Robsel
text:
🍲 Wintersuppe – Immunbooster für den Winter

Zutaten (für ca. 4 Portionen / 1 großer Topf)
🥔 Kartoffeln – 400 g
🥕 Möhren – 300 g
🌿 Fenchel – 200 g
🥬 Lauch – 150 g
🥔 Knollensellerie – 150 g
🧅 Rote Zwiebel – 1 große (~150 g)
🧄 Knoblauch – 3 Zehen
🌱 Frischer Ingwer – 2 cm Stück
🌿 Petersilie – 1 Handvoll
🌿 Brennnessel – 1 kleine Handvoll
🖤 Schwarzer Sesam – 1–2 EL
🍗 Knochenbrühe – 500 ml
💧 Wasser – 1,5 l

Zubereitung
Zwiebel in Kokosöl oder Ghee glasig anschwitzen.
Kartoffeln, Möhren, Knollensellerie, Fenchel, Lauch, Ingwer und Knoblauch dazugeben und kurz anrösten.
Mit Wasser und Knochenbrühe aufgießen, 20–25 Minuten köcheln, bis alles weich ist.
Petersilie und Brennnessel unterrühren, wenn die Suppe etwas abgekühlt ist.
Mit schwarzem Sesam toppen und genießen.

💡 Tipp:
In der TCM gilt eine warme Suppe als ideal, um die Verdauung zu unterstützen, den Körper zu erwärmen und überschüssigen Schleim auszuscheiden. Perfekt also für kalte Wintertage!

How do the horizontal lines on our face connect to the way we bring in Qi—our life force energy—into the body?

Qi is the universal energy that animates us. Jing, our inherited energy, is like the reserve battery we’re born with. When Qi becomes depleted, the Jing can get “frozen” in the face, showing up as fine lines or horizontal creases.

🍓 Bridge of the nose: if there’s a line here, it points to digestion and how we assimilate nourishment. Strengthening the gut and aligning meals with your body’s natural rhythms can help draw more Qi into the body.

🕊️ Philtrum (the space between the nose and upper lip): lines here reflect lung energy and breath capacity. Conscious breathing, movement, and slowing down can restore flow to this area.

🧘‍♀️ Below the lower lip: if there’s a line here, it often means you’ve been in overdrive—too much Yang energy—and your body is calling for rest, Yin nourishment, and perhaps a shift in pace or priorities.

Every line tells a story of how energy has moved through you—and how it wants to move again.

👉 To punkt, który wpływa na napięcie żuchwy, nerwy twarzy, równowagę emocjonalną i jakość snu. Pracuje się z nim, gdy ciało jest przebodźcowane, myśli krążą bez końca, a mięśnie twarzy są zaciśnięte od stresu.

👉 Regularny masaż tego punktu wycisza układ limbiczny, obniża pobudzenie i pomaga wrócić do regulacji autonomicznej.

👉 Jak zlokalizować ten punkt?
Punkt znajduje się w linii środkowej, dokładnie pod wargą dolną, w małym zagłębieniu nad brodą, tam gdzie kończy się dziąsło dolne. Lokalizuje się go palcem wskazującym – punkt reaguje delikatnym impulsem lub uczuciem rozluźnienia.

👉 Jak masować punkt?
Masaż wykonuje się opuszką palca wskazującego lub kciuka. Należy delikatnie uciskać punkt przez 20–30 sekund, a następnie wykonywać małe, powolne kółka. Cała sesja trwa od jednej do trzech minut. Nacisk powinien być średni, niebolesny, ale wyraźny. Oddychanie spokojne i rytmiczne.

👉 Pięć dobrych rad:
1. Masuj punkt Ren Mai 24 wieczorem. To przesyła do autonomicznego układu nerwowego sygnał, że pora przejść z trybu walki w tryb regeneracji.
2. Stosuj masaż, gdy czujesz napięcie w twarzy. Twarz jest pierwszym miejscem, które reaguje na stres, dlatego dotyk w tej okolicy szybko przywraca równowagę.
3. Łącz nacisk z powolnym wydechem. Wydech wydłuża sygnał do nerwu błędnego, a punkt wzmacnia ten efekt.
4. Używaj tego punktu przy przeciążeniu psychicznym. Napięcie żuchwy jest jednym z markerów nadmiernego pobudzenia układu limbicznego.

5. Łącz masaż punktu z ciepłem. Krótki, ciepły okład na okolice twarzy pogłębia rozluźnienie mięśniowe i wzmacnia efekt.

Paired with herbs like Shu Dì Huáng (Rehmannia) for mood-regulation and increasing cognitive function, the formula doesn’t just warm, it restores the root. (Note: this toxic herb, even more than most TCM herbs, should never be taken on its own. It must be balanced properly in a formula and ONLY taken in very small doses.)

Today, Jin Kui Shen Qi’s relevance hasn’t faded. A 2022 Frontiers in Pharmacology study found that it improved renal function and mitochondrial activity, suggesting protective effects against aging and metabolic burnout. Another study in Chinese Journal of Integrated Medicine reported its ability to modulate the HPA axis, linking it to stress resilience and endocrine health.

In modern language, this formula supports those burned out by years of overwork—not just tired, but constitutionally depleted. But unlike stimulants, this doesn’t stimulate, but nourishes and rebuilds. It is a medicine that sees fatigue not as weakness, but as a call to re-anchor the body’s deepest reserves.

Every woman carries an elemental blueprint — a pattern the ancient physicians of Chinese Medicine used to understand personality, health, emotions, beauty, and even the way a woman moves through the world. 

The Five Elements aren’t “mystical labels”; they’re a physiological-energetic model of how life expresses itself through you. Wood gives you direction. Fire gives you charisma. Earth gives you stability. Metal gives you refinement. Water gives you depth.

When your primary element is balanced, life feels aligned: your hormones respond better, your digestion is smoother, your mind is clearer, and your relationships feel easier. 

When that element slips out of balance, the body starts whispering — sometimes as PMS, bloating, burnout, skin changes, irritability, anxiety, or sudden waves of fatigue. TCM has always taught that before symptoms appear in the body, they first appear in the element.

You might see yourself in more than one. Most women do. Elements shift through seasons, hormones, motherhood, stress levels, and age. The goal isn’t to “pick one.” The goal is to understand the patterns that guide your health, your emotions, and your feminine energy.

Tell me in the comments: which element feels most like you right now? 🔥💧🌱🪨🪙

Moksa to jedna z najmniej znanych, a jednocześnie najpotężniejszych technik w Medycynie Chińskiej.
Nie kłuje. Nie boli. A potrafi zdziałać więcej, niż niejeden zabieg.

👉 Masuj Pęcherzyk żółciowy 1, gdy oczy są zmęczone, głowa ciężka, a napięcie zbiera się w skroniach. To mały punkt o dużej mocy regulacji.

👉 Gdzie jest ten punkt?
Punkt Pęcherzyk żółciowy 1 znajduje się przy zewnętrznym kąciku oka. Leży tuż za kącikiem, lekko na zewnątrz, w małym zagłębieniu między krawędzią oczodołu a skronią.
Najprościej go znaleźć, gdy zamkniesz oczy, położysz opuszki palców przy zewnętrznym kąciku oka i przesuniesz je o milimetr na zewnątrz w stronę skroni. Tam, gdzie czujesz małe, delikatne wgłębienie, znajduje się ten punkt.

👉 Jak masować Pęcherzyk żółciowy 1?
• Masuj zawsze bardzo delikatnie, ponieważ okolica oka jest wrażliwa.
• Zamknij oczy, rozluźnij twarz i szyję.
